column9: Go out, away from the speaker: 出去玩 'go out for fun', 我出去一下 'I'll step out'. After a verb it adds the outward direction: 跑出去, 拿出去 'take out'. The 土 on top of 去 is a man shape simplified, as in 赤 and 走.

column3: Sit down, a change of posture. 请坐下 is the polite command; 坐着 describes staying seated, which 坐下 does not. The opposite is 站起来.
column9: Sit down, a change of posture. 請坐下 is the polite command; 坐著 describes staying seated, which 坐下 does not. The opposite is 站起來.

column3: Walking, as against riding or driving: 走路去, 走路上班. A verb plus an object, so 走了半小时路 splits it. 走 alone often means leave, which is why 走路 is the clear word for walking. 走 began as a picture of a running man, with 止 'foot' added later.
column9: Walking, as against riding or driving: 走路去, 走路上班. A verb plus an object, so 走了半小時路 splits it. 走 alone often means leave, which is why 走路 is the clear word for walking. 走 began as a picture of a running man, with 止 'foot' added later.

column3: Mostly met in compounds: 起床, 起来, 一起 'together', 起飞 'take off'. 从明天起 means from tomorrow on, and 起 counts incidents: 一起事故 'an accident'. Perhaps from a Sino-Tibetan word meaning 'to lift, raise, awake'.
column9: Mostly met in compounds: 起床, 起來, 一起 'together', 起飛 'take off'. 從明天起 means from tomorrow on, and 起 counts incidents: 一起事故 'an accident'. Perhaps from a Sino-Tibetan word meaning 'to lift, raise, awake'.

column3: Get up or stand up. After a verb or adjective it marks a start: 笑起来 'start laughing', 热起来 'warm up'. After a perception verb it gives a first impression: 看起来 'looks like'.
column9: Get up or stand up. After a verb or adjective it marks a start: 笑起來 'start laughing', 熱起來 'warm up'. After a perception verb it gives a first impression: 看起來 'looks like'.

column3: The all-purpose measure word, the safe guess when unsure: 一个人, 三个朋友. Many nouns insist on their own, like 本 for books and 张 for paper. 个 is half of 竹 'bamboo', and may have grown from counting bamboo stalks into a classifier for every noun.
column9: The all-purpose measure word, the safe guess when unsure: 一個人, 三個朋友. Many nouns insist on their own, like 本 for books and 張 for paper.

column3: Counts books and anything bound: 一本书, 一本词典, 两本课本. Single sheets take 张, and newspapers take 份. Say 本子 for a notebook.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le sān běn shū.
column9: Counts books and anything bound: 一本書, 一本詞典, 兩本課本. Single sheets take 張, and newspapers take 份. Say 本子 for a notebook.

column3: A cup or glass, and the measure for what fills it: 一杯茶, 一杯水. 杯子 is the vessel itself, as in 茶杯 and 酒杯. 干杯 is 'bottoms up', the toast.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi shuǐ.
column7: Please give me a glass of water.
column9: A cup or glass, and the measure for what fills it: 一杯茶, 一杯水. 杯子 is the vessel itself, as in 茶杯 and 酒杯. 乾杯 is 'bottoms up', the toast.

column3: Counts occurrences, after the verb: 去过两次, 第一次. 遍 counts a whole run-through from start to end, so 读一遍 is read it all through. 次 also means second-rate, as in 次品. 次 is a person breathing out, the breath drawn as 二 or 冫 depending on the font.
column6: Wǒ qù guo liǎng cì Běijīng.
column7: I have been to Beijing twice.
column9: Counts occurrences, after the verb: 去過兩次, 第一次. 遍 counts a whole run-through from start to end, so 讀一遍 is read it all through. 次 also means second-rate, as in 次品. 次 is a person breathing out, the breath drawn as 二 or 冫 depending on the font.

column3: A bag (书包, 背包) or a wrapped thing (面包 bread, 包子 bun). As a verb it wraps or reserves the whole: 包饺子 'make dumplings', 包车 'charter a car'.
column6: Wǒ de bāo zài zhuōzi shang.
column7: My bag is on the table.
column9: A bag (書包, 背包) or a wrapped thing (麵包 bread, 包子 bun). As a verb it wraps or reserves the whole: 包餃子 'make dumplings', 包車 'charter a car'.

column3: The measure word for pieces ("一块肉") and, in speech, for money: 三块钱 "three yuan". 土 (earth) is the meaning part and 夬 the sound.
column9: The measure word for pieces ("一塊肉") and, in speech, for money: 三塊錢 "three yuan". 土 (earth) is the meaning part and 鬼 the sound.

column3: The written unit of money on prices and receipts: 20元; aloud people say 块. It also means 'first' in 元旦, New Year's Day, and 元月, January. Possibly from a Sino-Tibetan word for 'head'; Tibetan མགོ means 'head; summit; beginning'.
column9: The written unit of money on prices and receipts: 20元; aloud people say 塊. It also means 'first' in 元旦, New Year's Day, and 元月, January. Possibly from a Sino-Tibetan word for 'head'; Tibetan མགོ means 'head; summit; beginning'.

column3: In speech a tenth of a yuan: 五毛 is 0.5 yuan. In print and on price tags that unit is written 角. Small sums drop the unit: 三块五 'three fifty'. 毛 is also fur or body hair, as in 羽毛 and 毛衣.
column9: In speech a tenth of a yuan: 五毛 is 0.5 yuan. In print and on price tags that unit is written 角. Small sums drop the unit: 三塊五 'three fifty'. 毛 is also fur or body hair, as in 羽毛 and 毛衣.

column3: On the clock 分 follows the number: 三点十分. A length of time is 分钟: 十分钟. It is also a point in a score (九十分) and a hundredth of a yuan.
column9: On the clock 分 follows the number: 三點十分. A length of time is 分鐘: 十分鐘. It is also a point in a score (九十分) and a hundredth of a yuan.

column3: The everyday word for money in general: 花钱 'spend', 赚钱 'earn', 零钱 'small change', 多少钱 'how much'. 块 is the spoken yuan, and 钱 may follow it: 五块 and 五块钱 are the same.
column7: He has a lot of money.
column9: The everyday word for money in general: 花錢 'spend', 賺錢 'earn', 零錢 'small change', 多少錢 'how much'. 塊 is the spoken yuan, and 錢 may follow it: 五塊 and 五塊錢 are the same.

column3: A wallet or a purse, for either sex. On a phone, 钱包 is also the payment app's stored balance, as in 电子钱包 'e-wallet'. In Taiwan a bill-fold is often 皮夹.
column9: A wallet or a purse, for either sex. On a phone, 錢包 is also the payment app's stored balance, as in 電子錢包 'e-wallet'. In Taiwan a bill-fold is often 皮夾.

column3: Age goes after the number: 二十岁. Ask a child 你几岁？ and an adult 你多大？ A span of time is 年, not 岁: 三年 is three years, 三岁 is three years old.
column7: My son is three years old.
column9: Age goes after the number: 二十歲. Ask a child 你幾歲？ and an adult 你多大？ A span of time is 年, not 歲: 三年 is three years, 三歲 is three years old.

column3: Some, a few: 一些人, 一些书, with no measure word. 些 is the plural measure also seen in 这些 and 那些. For a small amount of something uncountable, 一点儿 is used.
column7: There are some books on the table.
column9: Some, a few: 一些人, 一些書, with no measure word. 些 is the plural measure also seen in 這些 and 那些. For a small amount of something uncountable, 一點兒 is used.

column3: A little: 一点儿水. After an adjective it gives 'a bit more': 快一点儿, and in a negative 'not at all': 一点儿也不累. Northern mainland speech adds the 儿 (yīdiǎnr); in Taiwan and the south people say 一点. Here 儿 is a diminutive suffix with no syllable of its own.
column7: Please speak a little more slowly.
column9: A little: 一點兒水. After an adjective it gives 'a bit more': 快一點兒, and in a negative 'not at all': 一點兒也不累. Northern mainland speech adds the 兒 (yīdiǎnr); in Taiwan and the south people say 一點. Here 兒 is a diminutive suffix with no syllable of its own.

column3: After a verb it makes the action brief, casual or a try: 看一下儿, 等一下儿. Alone, 一下子 is 'all at once'. Northern mainland speech adds the 儿 (yīxiàr); in Taiwan and the south people say 一下. The 儿 only adds an r to the end of 下: a diminutive suffix, not read er.
column9: After a verb it makes the action brief, casual or a try: 看一下兒, 等一下兒. Alone, 一下子 is 'all at once'. Northern mainland speech adds the 兒 (yīxiàr); in Taiwan and the south people say 一下. The 兒 only adds an r to the end of 下: a diminutive suffix, not read er.

column3: Before a noun it starts a subject: 有些人. Before an adjective it softens it: 有些累, 有些贵. For 'some... others...' the pair is 有的. The tale that 有 is a hand holding meat is folk etymology: the oracle bone script shows no meat.
column9: Before a noun it starts a subject: 有些人. Before an adjective it softens it: 有些累, 有些貴. For 'some... others...' the pair is 有的. The tale that 有 is a hand holding meat is folk etymology: the oracle bone script shows no meat.

column3: 'There are some' before a noun, or 'a little' before an adjective: 有一些辣. Fuller and a touch more emphatic than 有些. 些 is itself a classifier for a small amount.
column7: This dish is a bit spicy.
column9: 'There are some' before a noun, or 'a little' before an adjective: 有一些辣. Fuller and a touch more emphatic than 有些. 些 is itself a classifier for a small amount.

column3: Before a verb 很少 means 'seldom': 他很少来. As a verb 少 means to lack: 少了一个人 'one person is missing'. 少吃 is eat less, and 多吃 is the opposite.
column9: Before a verb 很少 means 'seldom': 他很少來. As a verb 少 means to lack: 少了一個人 'one person is missing'. 少吃 is eat less, and 多吃 is the opposite.

column3: 'Many' needs a degree word: 很多人, 好多人, not a bare 多 before the noun. Before an adjective it asks degree: 多大, 多远. After a number it means 'odd': 三十多岁. 多 is two pieces of meat, not two evenings: 肉 was worn down to 夕 in the bronze script.
column9: 'Many' needs a degree word: 很多人, 好多人, not a bare 多 before the noun. Before an adjective it asks degree: 多大, 多遠. After a number it means 'odd': 三十多歲. 多 is two pieces of meat, not two evenings: 肉 was worn down to 夕 in the bronze script.

column3: Together, the same as 一起: 我们一块儿去. It is spoken and northern; 一起 works anywhere and is the safe choice. 块 on its own is a lump or piece, and colloquially the yuan.
column9: Together, the same as 一起: 我們一塊兒去. It is spoken and northern; 一起 works anywhere and is the safe choice. 塊 on its own is a lump or piece, and colloquially the yuan.

column3: Half of something, and a noun, so no measure word follows: 吃了一半. For time spans 半 goes in front of the measure instead: 半年, 半个小时. 一半一半 is fifty-fifty. 半 is 八 'to divide' plus a cow 牛: to cut a cow into two halves.
column9: Half of something, and a noun, so no measure word follows: 吃了一半. For time spans 半 goes in front of the measure instead: 半年, 半個小時. 一半一半 is fifty-fifty. 半 is 八 'to divide' plus a cow 牛: to cut a cow into two halves.

column3: Counts shops and companies, not people: 一家商店. As a suffix it names a specialist: 作家, 画家, 科学家. 大家 is 'everyone'. The 豕 below the roof is a later corruption of an older sound part, 𢑓, which meant a male pig.
column9: Counts shops and companies, not people: 一家商店. As a suffix it names a specialist: 作家, 畫家, 科學家. 大家 is 'everyone'. The 豕 below the roof is a later corruption of an older sound part, 𢑓, which meant a male pig.

column3: Being at home, a state: 他在家. Going home is 回家. 在家办公 is working from home. In a Buddhist sense 在家 is a layperson, as against 出家, who becomes a monk. In early writing 在 was 才 borrowed for its sound; 士 was added later and eventually corrupted into 土.
column9: Being at home, a state: 他在家. Going home is 回家. 在家辦公 is working from home. In a Buddhist sense 在家 is a layperson, as against 出家, who becomes a monk. In early writing 在 was 才 borrowed for its sound; 士 was added later and eventually corrupted into 土.

column3: A place word for 'at home': 家里有人吗？ Used alone it is the place; 在家里 adds 在, while 在家 drops 里. 家里人 means the family members.
column7: There are a lot of books at home.
column9: A place word for 'at home': 家裡有人嗎？ Used alone it is the place; 在家裡 adds 在, while 在家 drops 裡. 家裡人 means the family members.

column3: The house or apartment as property: 买房子, 租房子, with 套 for a flat (一套房子) and 栋 for a building. A room inside is 房间. The sound part 方 'side' can add meaning too, if 房 first meant one of the two rooms beside the central room. Here 子 is a noun suffix, read light.
column9: The house or apartment as property: 買房子, 租房子, with 套 for a flat (一套房子) and 棟 for a building. A room inside is 房間. The sound part 方 'side' can add meaning too, if 房 first meant one of the two rooms beside the central room. Here 子 is a noun suffix, read light.

column3: A room inside a building, such as a hotel room: 订一个房间 'book a room'. The whole building is 房子, and 间 alone also counts rooms: 一间房.
column6: Wǒ de fángjiān zài èr lóu.
column7: My room is on the second floor.
column9: A room inside a building, such as a hotel room: 訂一個房間 'book a room'. The whole building is 房子, and 間 alone also counts rooms: 一間房.

column3: A polite word for the toilet, and the one to use when asking: 洗手间在哪儿？ 厕所 is the plain word and can sound blunt. 洗手 alone can also be a euphemism for it.
column9: A polite word for the toilet, and the one to use when asking: 洗手間在哪兒？ 廁所 is the plain word and can sound blunt. 洗手 alone can also be a euphemism for it.

column3: Counts rooms: 一间房, 一间教室. It ends words for spaces and spans: 房间, 时间, 中间, 空间, 洗手间. 间 is a variant of an older character meaning 'space, gap', with 日 'day' in place of 月 'moon'.
column6: Zhè ge fángzi yǒu sān jiān fáng.
column9: Counts rooms: 一間房, 一間教室. It ends words for spaces and spans: 房間, 時間, 中間, 空間, 洗手間. 間 is a variant of an older character meaning 'space, gap', with 日 'day' in place of 月 'moon'.

column3: Beyond doors, 门 counts school subjects and skills: 一门课, 一门外语. Opening and closing a door are 开门 and 关门. 门 is a picture of a gate, and 户 'door' is half of it.
column9: Beyond doors, 門 counts school subjects and skills: 一門課, 一門外語. Opening and closing a door are 開門 and 關門. 門 is a picture of a gate, and 戶 'door' is half of it.

column3: The area at a door or gate, inside or out: 站在门口 'stand in the doorway', 学校门口 'in front of the school gate'. The same 口 ends 出口 and 入口, exit and entrance.
column6: Xuéxiào ménkǒu yǒu yī ge shāngdiàn.
column7: There is a shop at the school entrance.
column9: The area at a door or gate, inside or out: 站在門口 'stand in the doorway', 學校門口 'in front of the school gate'. The same 口 ends 出口 and 入口, exit and entrance.

column3: A bed: 一张床, 在床上. 床 is also the measure word for quilts and blankets: 一床被子. Related words: 床单 'sheet', 起床 'get up'. An older form of 床 was built on 爿, which was itself the word for bed; 木 was added later.
column9: A bed: 一張床, 在床上. 床 is also the measure word for quilts and blankets: 一床被子. Related words: 床單 'sheet', 起床 'get up'. An older form of 床 was built on 爿, which was itself the word for bed; 木 was added later.

column3: Getting out of bed, as against 醒 'wake up'. A verb plus an object, so the 了 slides inside: 起了床. 起不了床 means cannot get out of bed.
column9: Getting out of bed, as against 醒 'wake up'. A verb plus an object, so the 了 slides inside: 起了床. 起不了床 means cannot get out of bed.

column3: Table, desk: 一张桌子; 桌子上 "on the table". 木 (wood) is the meaning part of 桌. The 子 is light: zhuōzi.
column7: The book is on the table.
column9: Table, desk: 一張桌子; 桌子上 "on the table". 木 (wood) is the meaning part of 桌. The 子 is light: zhuōzi.

column3: Building of several floors, and "floor": 二楼 is the second floor. 木 (wood) is the meaning part and 娄 gives the sound; both are lóu.
column7: My home is on the third floor.
column9: Building of several floors, and "floor": 二樓 is the second floor. 木 (wood) is the meaning part and 婁 gives the sound; both are lóu.

column3: Upstairs, relative to where you are: 楼上的邻居 'the neighbor above'. In forum threads 楼上 is also the poster just above you.
column9: Upstairs, relative to where you are: 樓上的鄰居 'the neighbor above'. In forum threads 樓上 is also the poster just above you.

column3: Downstairs, or the ground just outside the building: 在楼下等你 can mean waiting at the building's entrance, not on a lower floor. The pair is 楼上.
column9: Downstairs, or the ground just outside the building: 在樓下等你 can mean waiting at the building's entrance, not on a lower floor. The pair is 樓上.

column3: Live or stay: 住在北京, 住酒店 'stay at a hotel', 住三天. After a verb 住 means firmly or stopped: 站住 'halt', 记住 'remember', 拿住 'hold on to'.
column9: Live or stay: 住在北京, 住酒店 'stay at a hotel', 住三天. After a verb 住 means firmly or stopped: 站住 'halt', 記住 'remember', 拿住 'hold on to'.

column3: After a noun it means 'on': 桌子上. As a verb it means go to or get on: 上班, 上课, 上车. 上网 is to go online, and 上 for 'last' is in 上个月 'last month'.
column7: Class is starting, please sit down.
column9: After a noun it means 'on': 桌子上. As a verb it means go to or get on: 上班, 上課, 上車. 上網 is to go online, and 上 for 'last' is in 上個月 'last month'.

column3: Mirror of 上: get off or finish (下车, 下班, 下课), and rain or snow falls: 下雨, 下雪. 下次 is next time. After a verb 一下 softens it. 下 is related to 落, 'to fall, to drop'.
column9: Mirror of 上: get off or finish (下車, 下班, 下課), and rain or snow falls: 下雨, 下雪. 下次 is next time. After a verb 一下 softens it. 下 is related to 落, 'to fall, to drop'.

column3: After a noun it means 'in': 书包里, 城里, 家里. 里面 is the fuller 'inside', and 外面 is the opposite.
column7: The book is in the schoolbag.
column9: After a noun it means 'in': 書包裡, 城裡, 家裡. 裡面 is the fuller 'inside', and 外面 is the opposite.

column3: After a noun it marks the outside of it (门外, 城外), and 外 also builds 外国 and 外语. The opposite is 里. In the oracle-bone script 外 was written just like 卜; the bar reaching outward told them apart.
column7: There is someone outside the door.
column9: After a noun it marks the outside of it (門外, 城外), and 外 also builds 外國 and 外語. The opposite is 裡. In the oracle-bone script 外 was written just like 卜; the bar reaching outward told them apart.

column3: After a noun it is a place (门前); after a time it means ago (三年前); before a noun it means previous or former, as in 前天 and 前男友. It began as a foot on a boat moving forward; the 月 in it is a worn-down boat 舟, not the moon.
column6: Sān nián qián wǒ zhù zài Běijīng.
column7: Three years ago I lived in Beijing.
column9: After a noun it is a place (門前); after a time it means ago (三年前); before a noun it means previous or former, as in 前天 and 前男友. It began as a foot on a boat moving forward; the 月 in it is a worn-down boat 舟, not the moon.

column3: Behind, after: 门后, 三年后 "in three years".
column6: Sān nián hòu wǒ èrshí suì.
column7: In three years I will be twenty.
column9: Behind, after: 門後, 三年後 "in three years". 後 has a step 彳 and a foot 夂 held back by a thread 幺, "lagging behind".

column3: Besides 左边, it is in 往左走 and 左手, and 左右 after a number means about: 三十岁左右. Politically it is the left wing. It began as a picture of a left hand, and 工 was added in later bronze forms.
column9: Besides 左邊, it is in 往左走 and 左手, and 左右 after a number means about: 三十歲左右. Politically it is the left wing. It began as a picture of a left hand, and 工 was added in later bronze forms.

column3: A bound form, mostly in compounds like 右边, 右手 and 往右转; alone as a plain word you would say 右边. In bronze inscriptions a meaningless 口 was added to 右 as a distinguishing mark.
column9: A bound form, mostly in compounds like 右邊, 右手 and 往右轉; alone as a plain word you would say 右邊. In bronze inscriptions a meaningless 口 was added to 右 as a distinguishing mark.

column3: 东西 is two words: dōngxi, with a light xi, is a thing, and dōngxī is east and west. 东 also means the host or landlord, as in 房东. The tale of the sun rising behind a tree is probably a folk etymology: the oldest form pictured something tied at both ends.
column9: 東西 is two words: dōngxi, with a light xi, is a thing, and dōngxī is east and west. 東 also means the host or landlord, as in 房東. The tale of the sun rising behind a tree is probably a folk etymology: the oldest form pictured something tied at both ends.

column3: 东西 can mean east and west or, with a light xi, a thing. 西 is also the West, as in 西餐 and 西方, and the start of 西班牙, Spain. Early forms have been read as a bird's nest, possibly related to 栖.
column6: Wǎng xī zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào.
column7: Walk five minutes west and you are there.
column9: 東西 can mean east and west or, with a light xi, a thing. 西 is also the West, as in 西餐 and 西方, and the start of 西班牙, Spain. Early forms have been read as a bird's nest, possibly related to 棲.

column3: The compass points run 东南西北 in Chinese, never north-south first. 南方 is the south as a region, and 南 is also a surname. South has long been linked with the sun and light.
column9: The compass points run 東南西北 in Chinese, never north-south first. 南方 is the south as a region, and 南 is also a surname. South has long been linked with the sun and light.

column3: North: 北边, 北京 "northern capital". It is two people back to back; the word first meant "back", and "north" came from that.
column7: The school is north of the shop.
column9: North: 北邊, 北京 "northern capital". It is two people back to back; the word first meant "back", and "north" came from that.

column3: Besides the middle, it is China in 中国 and 中文, and 在…中 means within: 在雨中 in the rain. It is a flagpole, and its middle box has been read as a drum.
column9: Besides the middle, it is China in 中國 and 中文, and 在…中 means within: 在雨中 in the rain. It is a flagpole, and its middle box has been read as a drum.

column3: It names the spot right next to something: 在…旁边, 我旁边, 旁边的人. 附近 is nearby, on a wider scale. Alone, 旁 also names the side component of a character, such as 亻.
column9: It names the spot right next to something: 在…旁邊, 我旁邊, 旁邊的人. 附近 is nearby, on a wider scale. Alone, 旁 also names the side component of a character, such as 亻.

column3: It means between two or more things (两个人中间) or the middle of one (房间中间). 之间 follows two named things or a group (朋友之间) and is more written. Read jiàn, 间 means a gap, or to separate and sow discontent.
column6: Shūdiàn zài liǎng ge shāngdiàn zhōngjiān.
column7: The bookshop is between two shops.
column9: It means between two or more things (兩個人中間) or the middle of one (房間中間). 之間 follows two named things or a group (朋友之間) and is more written. Read jiàn, 間 means a gap, or to separate and sow discontent.

column3: A place word; in text it can mean above-mentioned: 上边说的. 上面 means the same. 上 puts a short stroke above a long one, and 下 the short stroke below it.
column7: Your name is at the top.
column9: A place word; in text it can mean above-mentioned: 上邊說的. 上面 means the same. 上 puts a short stroke above a long one, and 下 the short stroke below it.

column3: Under or below. In a text it points to what follows: 下边的例子, the example below. 下 mirrors 上: its short stroke sits below the long one.
column7: The book is under the table.
column9: Under or below. In a text it points to what follows: 下邊的例子, the example below. 下 mirrors 上: its short stroke sits below the long one.

column3: Inside, as a place word: 房间里边. 里面 means the same, and 里 alone after a noun is the plainer 房间里.
column9: Inside, as a place word: 房間裡邊. 裡面 means the same, and 裡 alone after a noun is the plainer 房間裡.

column3: Outside, but also abroad or anywhere away from home: 他在外边吃饭 means he eats out.
column9: Outside, but also abroad or anywhere away from home: 他在外邊吃飯 means he eats out.

column3: A place word, in front or ahead: 在学校前边, 前边有一家商店. 前面 is just as common. 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.
column7: There is a shop up ahead.
column9: A place word, in front or ahead: 在學校前邊, 前邊有一家商店. 前面 is just as common. 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.

column3: A place word, behind or at the back: 在我后边, 后边的人. It can also be the later part of something, as in 后边的几页. Alone, 后 is also an empress or queen, a word for a ruler.
column9: A place word, behind or at the back: 在我後邊, 後邊的人. It can also be the later part of something, as in 後邊的幾頁. Alone, 後 is also an empress or queen, a word for a ruler.

column3: The left side or to the left of: 在门左边, 往左边走. The pair is 右边; 左右 after a number means about. 左 began as a picture of a left hand.
column7: My home is to the left of the school.
column9: The left side or to the left of: 在門左邊, 往左邊走. The pair is 右邊; 左右 after a number means about. 左 began as a picture of a left hand.

column3: The right side: 坐在我右边, 往右边走. Its partner is 左边. In older writing 右 is the side of precedence.
column7: The teacher sits on my right.
column9: The right side: 坐在我右邊, 往右邊走. Its partner is 左邊. In older writing 右 is the side of precedence.

column3: A place word: 学校东边 is east of the school, and 东边 alone is the east side. Compass points run 东南西北.
column7: There is a train station on the east side.
column9: A place word: 學校東邊 is east of the school, and 東邊 alone is the east side. Compass points run 東南西北.

column3: West side. This dictionary gives 西边 a full first tone on 边: xībiān. The compass order in Chinese is 东南西北, so west comes third.
column7: To the west there are mountains.
column9: West side. This dictionary gives 西邊 a full first tone on 邊: xībiān. The compass order in Chinese is 東南西北, so west comes third.

column3: The south side or south of: 学校南边, or the south as a region: 南边的城市. 南 is second in 东南西北. South has long been linked with the sun and light.
column7: My home is in the south.
column9: The south side or south of: 學校南邊, or the south as a region: 南邊的城市. 南 is second in 東南西北. South has long been linked with the sun and light.

column3: The north side or north of: 学校北边, 北边的天气. 北 is last in 东南西北. 北 shows two people back to back, and 'north' grew from 'back': the back faces north when you face south.
column6: Xuéxiào běibiān yǒu yī jiā shūdiàn.
column7: North of the school there is a bookshop.
column9: The north side or north of: 學校北邊, 北邊的天氣. 北 is last in 東南西北. 北 shows two people back to back, and 'north' grew from 'back': the back faces north when you face south.

column3: Put 一边 before each of two verbs done at once: 一边吃一边说. Alone it is one side, or, in pairs, on the one hand and on the other.
column6: Tā yībiān zǒulù yībiān tīng gē.
column7: He listens to songs while he walks.
column9: Put 一邊 before each of two verbs done at once: 一邊吃一邊說. Alone it is one side, or, in pairs, on the one hand and on the other.

column3: It covers watch (看电影), read (看书), visit (看朋友) and see a doctor (看病); after a verb it means try: 尝尝看. 我看 also opens an opinion. It is a hand above the eyes, gazing afar.
column9: It covers watch (看電影), read (看書), visit (看朋友) and see a doctor (看病); after a verb it means try: 嘗嘗看. 我看 also opens an opinion. It is a hand above the eyes, gazing afar.

column3: It is listen (听歌, 听老师说) and also obey: 听话 is to be obedient. A can of drink is 一听可乐 on the mainland, from English tin; Taiwan says 一罐可乐.
column9: It is listen (聽歌, 聽老師說) and also obey: 聽話 is to be obedient. A can of drink is 一聽可樂 on the mainland, from English tin; Taiwan says 一罐可樂.

column3: It takes a language or what is said (说汉语, 说一句话) and can mean to scold: 他说了我一顿. As theory it is bound, as in 学说.
column9: It takes a language or what is said (說漢語, 說一句話) and can mean to scold: 他說了我一頓. As theory it is bound, as in 學說.

column3: It is to read aloud (读课文) and to study at a school: 读书, 读大学. For reading quietly, a book or a phone, 看 is the everyday verb. Its sense grew from saying aloud to reciting to reading.
column6: Qǐng dú yīxià zhè ge zì.
column9: It is to read aloud (讀課文) and to study at a school: 讀書, 讀大學. For reading quietly, a book or a phone, 看 is the everyday verb. Its sense grew from saying aloud to reciting to reading.

column3: It takes an object or a result: 写字, 写信, 写错了. It covers writing a letter, an essay or a song: 写歌.
column9: It takes an object or a result: 寫字, 寫信, 寫錯了. It covers writing a letter, an essay or a song: 寫歌.

column3: The person comes first: 问老师 or 问他一个问题. For a polite opener, 请问 means may I ask. Asking is, literally, letting me hear.
column6: Tā wèn wǒ jiào shénme míngzi.
column7: He asked me what my name is.
column9: The person comes first: 問老師 or 問他一個問題. For a polite opener, 請問 means may I ask. Asking is, literally, letting me hear.

column3: It is a verb and a noun: 回答问题, 他的回答. 一问一答 is one question, one answer. 回 began as a spiral, a picture of rotation.
column9: It is a verb and a noun: 回答問題, 他的回答. 一問一答 is one question, one answer. 回 began as a spiral, a picture of rotation.

column3: It is be called (我叫王明) and call or tell someone to (叫他来), and 叫车 is to hail a ride. In a passive sentence it can mean by.
column6: Wǒ jiào Wáng Míng, nǐ jiào shénme?
column7: My name is Wang Ming, what's yours?
column9: It is be called (我叫王明) and call or tell someone to (叫他來), and 叫車 is to hail a ride. In a passive sentence it can mean by.

column3: Name: 你叫什么名字？ In 名, one explanation is 夕 (evening) over 口 (mouth): saying your name to be known in the dark. In 字, 子 gives the sound. The 字 is light: míngzi.
column9: Name: 你叫什麼名字？ In 名, one explanation is 夕 (evening) over 口 (mouth): saying your name to be known in the dark. In 字, 子 gives the sound. The 字 is light: míngzi.

column3: The person follows directly: 告诉我, not 告诉对我. Its origin is unclear; one theory sees a tongue sticking out from the mouth.
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de míngzi.
column9: The person follows directly: 告訴我, not 告訴對我. Its origin is unclear; one theory sees a tongue sticking out from the mouth.

column3: The 到 says the seeing worked: 我看到他了, 没看到. It also covers what you read or notice: 我在新闻里看到. 看见 is more the eye catching it.
column6: Wǒ kàndào nǐ de lǎoshī le.
column9: The 到 says the seeing worked: 我看到他了, 沒看到. It also covers what you read or notice: 我在新聞裡看到. 看見 is more the eye catching it.

column3: The 见 says the sight reached you: 我看见他了, and 没看见 is did not see. 看 alone is only look. 见 began as a kneeling person with a huge eye for a head.
column6: Nǐ kànjiàn wǒ de qiánbāo le ma?
column9: The 見 says the sight reached you: 我看見他了, and 沒看見 is did not see. 看 alone is only look. 見 began as a kneeling person with a huge eye for a head.

column3: The 到 says the sound reached you: 我听到了, 没听到. It also covers news: 听到消息. 听 alone is only trying to listen.
column9: The 到 says the sound reached you: 我聽到了, 沒聽到. It also covers news: 聽到消息. 聽 alone is only trying to listen.

column3: The 见 says the sound reached you: 我听见有人叫我, 没听见. 听到 means the same; 听 alone is only trying to listen.
column9: The 見 says the sound reached you: 我聽見有人叫我, 沒聽見. 聽到 means the same; 聽 alone is only trying to listen.

column3: A verb and its object, so it splits: 说了很多话, 说句话. It also means to chat or, in older storytelling, to tell stories.
column9: A verb and its object, so it splits: 說了很多話, 說句話. It also means to chat or, in older storytelling, to tell stories.

column3: Study, go to school: 他在北京读书 "he studies in Beijing". It can also mean "read a book". 读 plus 书, "read" plus "book".
column9: Study, go to school: 他在北京讀書 "he studies in Beijing". It can also mean "read a book". 讀 plus 書, "read" plus "book".

column3: Dictation, a school exercise: 有听写, 做听写, 听写生词. It is also the verb for writing down what is read, and in music, transcribing by ear.
column9: Dictation, a school exercise: 有聽寫, 做聽寫, 聽寫生詞. It is also the verb for writing down what is read, and in music, transcribing by ear.

column3: It is both smile and laugh: 笑了, 爱笑, 笑起来. With a person it is laugh at: 笑他. A joke is 玩笑. The oldest form had 艸 and 犬; the later form uses 竹 and 夭.
column9: It is both smile and laugh: 笑了, 愛笑, 笑起來. With a person it is laugh at: 笑他. A joke is 玩笑. The oldest form had 艸 and 犬; the later form uses 竹 and 夭.

column3: Sing: 唱一首歌 "sing a song". 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 昌 the sound.
column6: Nǐ huì chàng zhè shǒu gē ma?
column9: Sing: 唱一首歌 "sing a song". 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 昌 the sound.

column3: A verb and its object, so it splits: 唱了一首歌, 唱一首歌. The measure word for a song is 首. 唱 alone can take a song or a style: 唱京剧. 唱 is the same word as 倡, to lead or advocate.
column9: A verb and its object, so it splits: 唱了一首歌, 唱一首歌. The measure word for a song is 首. 唱 alone can take a song or a style: 唱京劇. 唱 is the same word as 倡, to lead or advocate.

column3: Seldom alone: 看见, 再见, 见面, 见到. Alone it is a goodbye after a time (明天见!), or meet a person: 我见过他. 见 can also be an opinion. 见 began as a kneeling person with a huge eye for a head.
column9: Seldom alone: 看見, 再見, 見面, 見到. Alone it is a goodbye after a time (明天見!), or meet a person: 我見過他. 見 can also be an opinion. 見 began as a kneeling person with a huge eye for a head.

column3: A verb and its object, so nothing follows it: 跟朋友见面, not 见面朋友. It splits: 见过面, 见一面. 面 began as a face with one eye exaggerated.
column9: A verb and its object, so nothing follows it: 跟朋友見面, not 見面朋友. It splits: 見過面, 見一面. 面 began as a face with one eye exaggerated.

column3: It introduces people (介绍朋友), presents things (介绍情况) and recommends someone for a job. 把她介绍给你 puts the person first. 介 shows a person with two marks around: in between.
column4: 我来介绍一下，这是我的朋友。
column5: 我來介紹一下，這是我的朋友。
column6: Wǒ lái jièshào yīxià, zhè shì wǒ de péngyou.
column7: Let me introduce you, this is my friend.
column9: It introduces people (介紹朋友), presents things (介紹情況) and recommends someone for a job. 把她介紹給你 puts the person first. 介 shows a person with two marks around: in between.

column3: It is what is said, counted with 句: 一句话. It is the noun beside the verb 说: 说话, 电话, 谈话, 会话. The 舌 on the right of 话 is not related to the tongue 舌.
column9: It is what is said, counted with 句: 一句話. It is the noun beside the verb 說: 說話, 電話, 談話, 會話. The 舌 on the right of 話 is not related to the tongue 舌.

column3: Study, learn: 学汉语. 子 (child) is the bottom part of 学.
column9: Study, learn: 學漢語. 子 (child) is the bottom part of 學. In 學, two hands sit around 爻 and the 冖 was once 六; the child was added later.

column3: A pupil of any level, from primary school up. A fellow student is 同学, and teachers address the whole class as 同学们. 生 pictures a bud sprouting from the ground.
column6: Wǒmen bān yǒu èrshí ge xuésheng.
column9: A pupil of any level, from primary school up. A fellow student is 同學, and teachers address the whole class as 同學們. 生 pictures a bud sprouting from the ground.

column3: It is both a verb and a noun: 学习汉语, 他的学习很好. Alone, 学 is to learn a skill (学开车); 学习 is studying in general. 习 comes from wings 羽 over a sun 日: to learn to fly, to practice flying.
column7: He is studying in the library.
column9: It is both a verb and a noun: 學習漢語, 他的學習很好. Alone, 學 is to learn a skill (學開車); 學習 is studying in general. 習 comes from wings 羽 over a sun 日: to learn to fly, to practice flying.

column3: The school as a place or institution of any level: 我的学校, 在学校. Attending as a pupil is 上学. Read jiào, 校 means to check or proofread.
column9: The school as a place or institution of any level: 我的學校, 在學校. Attending as a pupil is 上學. Read jiào, 校 means to check or proofread.

column3: College, institute, school, faculty: 医学院 "medical school". 院 has 完 as sound part (wán against yuàn).
column7: He studies at the medical school.
column9: College, institute, school, faculty: 醫學院 "medical school". 院 has 完 as sound part (wán against yuàn).

column3: Go to university is 上大学; it covers colleges too. A 学院 is a college or institute, often inside a university. 大 is a person standing and facing forward; 人 is the same person in profile.
column7: He goes to university in Beijing.
column9: Go to university is 上大學; it covers colleges too. A 學院 is a college or institute, often inside a university. 大 is a person standing and facing forward; 人 is the same person in profile.

column3: Add 生 to a school level: 小学生, 中学生, 大学生. Others are 留学生, a student abroad, and 研究生, a graduate student.
column7: My older sister is a university student.
column9: Add 生 to a school level: 小學生, 中學生, 大學生. Others are 留學生, a student abroad, and 研究生, a graduate student.

column3: Primary school as a school and as a stage: 上小学, 我的小学. Next come 中学 and then 大学. 小 is three small dots in one reading, three grains of sand in another.
column7: My younger brother is in primary school.
column9: Primary school as a school and as a stage: 上小學, 我的小學. Next come 中學 and then 大學. 小 is three small dots in one reading, three grains of sand in another.

column3: A primary-school pupil, and figuratively a beginner: 我只是个小学生 means I am only a beginner.
column9: A primary-school pupil, and figuratively a beginner: 我只是個小學生 means I am only a beginner.

column3: It covers both stages of secondary school: the lower stage is 初中 on the mainland and 国中 in Taiwan, the upper stage 高中 in both. Before it come 小学 (elementary school), after it 大学 (university).
column7: I teach Chinese at a secondary school.
column9: It covers both stages of secondary school: the lower stage is 初中 on the mainland and 國中 in Taiwan, the upper stage 高中 in both. Before it come 小學 (elementary school), after it 大學 (university).

column3: Said of a pupil at either stage; to be exact, a lower-stage pupil is 初中生 on the mainland and 国中生 in Taiwan, an upper-stage one 高中生 in both. A university student is 大学生.
column9: Said of a pupil at either stage; to be exact, a lower-stage pupil is 初中生 on the mainland and 國中生 in Taiwan, an upper-stage one 高中生 in both. A university student is 大學生.

column3: About going to school as a routine, not one class (for that, 上课). 还在上学 says someone is still a student, and 上不起学 means cannot afford school.
column7: My younger brother goes to school at eight.
column9: About going to school as a routine, not one class (for that, 上課). 還在上學 says someone is still a student, and 上不起學 means cannot afford school.

column3: It is the end of the whole school day, while 下课 ends a single class. 放学后 is the usual way to say after school, and 几点放学 asks when school lets out.
column6: Fàngxué hòu wǒmen qù wánr ba.
column9: It is the end of the whole school day, while 下課 ends a single class. 放學後 is the usual way to say after school, and 幾點放學 asks when school lets out.

column3: The building with the classrooms on a school or university campus, as opposed to the dormitory (宿舍楼) or the library (图书馆). 教 is read jiào in this word, a bound form, while the verb on its own is jiāo.
column7: We have class in the classroom building.
column9: The building with the classrooms on a school or university campus, as opposed to the dormitory (宿舍樓) or the library (圖書館). 教 is read jiào in this word, a bound form, while the verb on its own is jiāo.

column3: Teach: teacher, then person, then subject: 她教我汉语. 攵 (a stick, the teaching cane) and 子 (child): teaching a child. Read jiāo when it stands alone as "teach"; inside words such as 教学楼 and 教育 it is jiào.
column9: Teach: teacher, then person, then subject: 她教我漢語. 攵 (a stick, the teaching cane) and 子 (child): teaching a child. Read jiāo when it stands alone as "teach"; inside words such as 教學樓 and 教育 it is jiào.

column3: A verb plus object, so it splits: 上了一节课, 上课时 (during class). Teacher and students both use it, one to teach a class and the other to attend it. 上学 is going to school at all.
column9: A verb plus object, so it splits: 上了一節課, 上課時 (during class). Teacher and students both use it, one to teach a class and the other to attend it. 上學 is going to school at all.

column3: The end of one class; 放学 is the end of the school day. 下课后 means after class.
column7: Class is over, let's go eat.
column9: The end of one class; 放學 is the end of the school day. 下課後 means after class.

column3: Counted with 节, one class period: 一节课, 两节课. In a textbook it numbers the lessons: 第三课. 上课 and 下课 begin and end it.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu sān jié kè.
column9: Counted with 節, one class period: 一節課, 兩節課. In a textbook it numbers the lessons: 第三課. 上課 and 下課 begin and end it.

column3: The book the class follows, in which each lesson's passage is a 课文. 请打开课本 is a teacher's stock instruction, often followed by a page number.
column9: The book the class follows, in which each lesson's passage is a 課文. 請打開課本 is a teacher's stock instruction, often followed by a page number.

column3: The passage a lesson is built around, which the class reads aloud, studies and often memorizes: 读课文, 背课文 (recite it from memory). Not any text; for an article, say 文章.
column9: The passage a lesson is built around, which the class reads aloud, studies and often memorizes: 讀課文, 背課文 (recite it from memory). Not any text; for an article, say 文章.

column3: Counted with 本: 一本书. 看书 is reading, and 读书 can also mean to study or be in school: 他还在读书.
column9: Counted with 本: 一本書. 看書 is reading, and 讀書 can also mean to study or be in school: 他還在讀書.

column3: The bag students carry their books in, usually on the back: 背书包. 包 is the general word for a bag, as in 钱包 and 手提包.
column9: The bag students carry their books in, usually on the back: 背書包. 包 is the general word for a bag, as in 錢包 and 手提包.

column3: A plain notebook for schoolwork or jotting, counted with 个 or 本. 笔记本 is the notebook meant for notes. 子 is a noun suffix here, read with a light tone.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng ge běnzi.
column9: A plain notebook for schoolwork or jotting, counted with 個 or 本. 筆記本 is the notebook meant for notes. 子 is a noun suffix here, read with a light tone.

column3: One written character, counted with 个: 汉字, 写字. A word is 词, not 字. It also means handwriting: 他的字很好看 says his handwriting is nice.
column7: How do you read this character?
column9: One written character, counted with 個: 漢字, 寫字. A word is 詞, not 字. It also means handwriting: 他的字很好看 says his handwriting is nice.

column3: Chinese characters: 汉 plus 字. 汉 is "Han"; it was first the name of the Han river, with 氵 (water) as its meaning part. 写汉字 is what this app practices.
column7: I am learning to write Chinese characters.
column9: Chinese characters: 漢 plus 字. 漢 is "Han"; it was first the name of the Han river, with 氵 (water) as its meaning part. 寫漢字 is what this app practices.

column3: On the mainland it is the name of the subject of study (汉语课, and the HSK, 汉语水平考试), while 中文 is the everyday word. In Taiwan 汉语 is hardly used: say 中文 (国语 is the official, more formal or older word), and 华语 for Chinese taught to foreigners.
column9: On the mainland it is the name of the subject of study (漢語課, and the HSK, 漢語水平考試), while 中文 is the everyday word. In Taiwan 漢語 is hardly used: say 中文 (國語 is the official, more formal or older word), and 華語 for Chinese taught to foreigners.

column3: The general word for Chinese, and the usual one for the written language: 学中文, 中文名字, 中文书. In Taiwan it is the everyday word for the spoken language too (说中文), with 国语 the official, more formal or older word, and 华语 is used when teaching foreigners; on the mainland 汉语 is also common.
column9: The general word for Chinese, and the usual one for the written language: 學中文, 中文名字, 中文書. In Taiwan it is the everyday word for the spoken language too (說中文), with 國語 the official, more formal or older word, and 華語 is used when teaching foreigners; on the mainland 漢語 is also common.

column3: The general word for foreign languages; to name one, say 英语, 日语, 法语. 外 marks other foreign things too: 外国人 (a foreigner), 外文 (a foreign-language text).
column7: What foreign language do you want to learn?
column9: The general word for foreign languages; to name one, say 英語, 日語, 法語. 外 marks other foreign things too: 外國人 (a foreigner), 外文 (a foreign-language text).

column3: It takes what is tested as its object: 考汉语, 考驾照, 考大学. The exam itself is 考试. It can also be done to someone: 老师考我们 means the teacher quizzes us.
column7: We have a Chinese test tomorrow.
column9: It takes what is tested as its object: 考漢語, 考駕照, 考大學. The exam itself is 考試. It can also be done to someone: 老師考我們 means the teacher quizzes us.

column3: Exam, test, and "to take an exam": 明天有考试; 考试了吗？ 试 has 讠 (speech) as meaning part and 式 as sound part, both shì.
column9: Exam, test, and "to take an exam": 明天有考試; 考試了嗎？ 試 has 言 (speech) as meaning part and 式 as sound part, both shì.

column3: Doubled or with 一下 it means give it a try: 试试, 试一下. It builds many words for trying something out: 试穿 (try on), 试吃 (taste a sample), 试用 (try out). 考试 is the exam.
column9: Doubled or with 一下 it means give it a try: 試試, 試一下. It builds many words for trying something out: 試穿 (try on), 試吃 (taste a sample), 試用 (try out). 考試 is the exam.

column3: The page of a book, with 第: 第三页, 第几页. It also builds 网页 (a web page) and 首页 (a home page).
column9: The page of a book, with 第: 第三頁, 第幾頁. It also builds 網頁 (a web page) and 首頁 (a home page).

column3: A class as a group that learns together: 我们班, 班长 (class leader), 同班同学 (classmates). It is also a work shift: 上班 is going to work, 下班 getting off work, 加班 working overtime.
column9: A class as a group that learns together: 我們班, 班長 (class leader), 同班同學 (classmates). It is also a work shift: 上班 is going to work, 下班 getting off work, 加班 working overtime.

column3: Three everyday senses: want to (我想去), miss someone (我很想你) and suppose (我想他不来了). As “want” it is softer than 要, a wish rather than a firm plan; 不想 turns something down gently. It comes from the word for “appearance”: appearance, then to visualize, then to think.
column9: Three everyday senses: want to (我想去), miss someone (我很想你) and suppose (我想他不來了). As “want” it is softer than 要, a wish rather than a firm plan; 不想 turns something down gently. It comes from the word for “appearance”: appearance, then to visualize, then to think.

column3: Stronger than 想: a decision or a need. 要…了 means about to: 要下雨了. 不要 means don't (不要走), while don't want to is 不想.
column7: I'll have a cup of tea.
column9: Stronger than 想: a decision or a need. 要…了 means about to: 要下雨了. 不要 means don't (不要走), while don't want to is 不想.

column3: A learned skill or know-how, where 能 is circumstance or permission: 他会游泳, 今天不能游泳. It also predicts: 明天会下雨, 他会来的 (he will surely come).
column9: A learned skill or know-how, where 能 is circumstance or permission: 他會游泳, 今天不能游泳. It also predicts: 明天會下雨, 他會來的 (he will surely come).

column3: Ability or possibility that depends on the situation, or permission: 这里不能抽烟 (no smoking here), 你明天能来吗？ A learned skill is 会. 不能 is cannot or may not.
column9: Ability or possibility that depends on the situation, or permission: 這裡不能抽煙 (no smoking here), 你明天能來嗎？ A learned skill is 會. 不能 is cannot or may not.

column3: Milder than 爱. It takes a noun (喜欢这本书) or goes straight onto a verb (喜欢看书). Degree words go before it: 很喜欢, 特别喜欢. 不喜欢 is dislike. 喜 is a drum plus a mouth.
column9: Milder than 愛. It takes a noun (喜歡這本書) or goes straight onto a verb (喜歡看書). Degree words go before it: 很喜歡, 特別喜歡. 不喜歡 is dislike. 喜 is a drum plus a mouth.

column3: Stronger than 喜欢, and used for people: 我爱你. Before a verb it means be fond of doing or tend to: 他爱吃肉, 她爱哭 (she cries easily).
column9: Stronger than 喜歡, and used for people: 我愛你. Before a verb it means be fond of doing or tend to: 他愛吃肉, 她愛哭 (she cries easily).

column3: The ordinary word for a hobby: 你有什么爱好？ A verb or noun can follow: 爱好游泳, 爱好音乐. 兴趣 is the looser interest. 好 is read hào here, to be fond of, not hǎo.
column9: The ordinary word for a hobby: 你有什麼愛好？ A verb or noun can follow: 愛好游泳, 愛好音樂. 興趣 is the looser interest. 好 is read hào here, to be fond of, not hǎo.

column3: 好 before a verb means good to do it: 好吃, 好喝, 好听, 好用. 好看 says something looks nice or is worth watching or reading: 好看的电影. 难看 is the opposite. 看 is a hand put above the eyes to gaze afar.
column7: This piece of clothing looks nice.
column9: 好 before a verb means good to do it: 好吃, 好喝, 好聽, 好用. 好看 says something looks nice or is worth watching or reading: 好看的電影. 難看 is the opposite. 看 is a hand put above the eyes to gaze afar.

column3: The same 好 plus verb pattern as 好吃 and 好看. It is for what you hear: a song, a voice, a name: 好听的歌, 声音好听. 难听 is the opposite.
column9: The same 好 plus verb pattern as 好吃 and 好看. It is for what you hear: a song, a voice, a name: 好聽的歌, 聲音好聽. 難聽 is the opposite.

column3: A mood in the moment: 很高兴认识你 is the stock phrase on meeting someone. Before a verb it means glad to do it: 我很高兴帮你。 兴 is read xìng here, as in “excitement”, and not xīng, “to rise”.
column7: I'm very glad to meet you.
column9: A mood in the moment: 很高興認識你 is the stock phrase on meeting someone. Before a verb it means glad to do it: 我很高興幫你。 興 is read xìng here, as in “excitement”, and not xīng, “to rise”.

column3: Get angry: 别生气 "don't be angry"; 生他的气 "be angry with him". 生 is "produce", and 气 here stands for 怒气 "anger": "produce anger". A verb and its object, so 生了气 splits it.
column9: Get angry: 別生氣 "don't be angry"; 生他的氣 "be angry with him". 生 is "produce", and 氣 here stands for 怒氣 "anger": "produce anger". A verb and its object, so 生了氣 splits it.

column3: A soft way to give an opinion: 我觉得 and then a whole clause, 我觉得这个很好. It is also for how you feel: 觉得冷, 觉得累. 觉 is read jué here, “to feel”.
column6: Wǒ juéde zhè ge hěn hǎo.
column7: I think this one is good.
column9: A soft way to give an opinion: 我覺得 and then a whole clause, 我覺得這個很好. It is also for how you feel: 覺得冷, 覺得累. 覺 is read jué here, “to feel”.

column3: Do, make: 做饭 "cook", 做什么 "do what". It began as a later variant of 作, and the two sound the same, zuò; today 做 is for doing and making things, and 作 is mostly found inside set words such as 工作 and 作业. 亻 (person) is the left part.
column9: Do, make: 做飯 "cook", 做什麼 "do what". It began as a later variant of 作, and the two sound the same, zuò; today 做 is for doing and making things, and 作 is mostly found inside set words such as 工作 and 作業. 亻 (person) is the left part.

column3: A spoken verb for doing or working: 干活, 干什么. In writing and in Taiwan, 做 is the safer verb, since the same sound is also a common vulgar word.
column9: A spoken verb for doing or working: 幹活, 幹什麼. In writing and in Taiwan, 做 is the safer verb, since the same sound is also a common vulgar word.

column3: The thing bought is the object: 买一本书, 买菜 (buy groceries), 买东西 (go shopping). Its opposite 卖 differs only by tone, so check which one you say. Its old form is a net over a money cowrie shell.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī běn shū.
column7: I want to buy a book.
column9: The thing bought is the object: 買一本書, 買菜 (buy groceries), 買東西 (go shopping). Its opposite 賣 differs only by tone, so check which one you say. Its old form is a net over a money cowrie shell.

column3: The all-purpose word for things: 买东西 is to shop, 吃东西 to eat something, 好东西 good stuff. Said of a person it is usually derogatory (不是东西), though 小东西 is affectionate and 坏东西 can be playful teasing.
column9: The all-purpose word for things: 買東西 is to shop, 吃東西 to eat something, 好東西 good stuff. Said of a person it is usually derogatory (不是東西), though 小東西 is affectionate and 壞東西 can be playful teasing.

column3: Anything held or picked up in the hand: 拿着, 拿起来, 拿出来 (take out), 拿走 (take away). For bringing something along with you, 带 is the usual verb.
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ ná yīxià shū.
column7: Please hold the book for me.
column9: Anything held or picked up in the hand: 拿著, 拿起來, 拿出來 (take out), 拿走 (take away). For bringing something along with you, 帶 is the usual verb.

column3: The same sense of letting go or setting out runs through 放假 (a holiday begins), 放心 (relax, stop worrying) and 放音乐 (play music). For putting something somewhere: 放在桌子上.
column9: The same sense of letting go or setting out runs through 放假 (a holiday begins), 放心 (relax, stop worrying) and 放音樂 (play music). For putting something somewhere: 放在桌子上.

column3: Not plain handing over, which is 给. 送 is a gift (送你一本书), going along to see someone off (送朋友去机场), or delivery, as in 送外卖 on the mainland and 外送 in Taiwan.
column6: Wǒ sòng nǐ yī běn shū.
column9: Not plain handing over, which is 給. 送 is a gift (送你一本書), going along to see someone off (送朋友去機場), or delivery, as in 送外賣 on the mainland and 外送 in Taiwan.

column3: Before a verb it names the tool or language: 用手机拍照, 用中文说. 不用 is no need, as in 不用谢. 请用 offers food or drink politely: 请用茶。
column9: Before a verb it names the tool or language: 用手機拍照, 用中文說. 不用 is no need, as in 不用謝. 請用 offers food or drink politely: 請用茶。

column3: Like 有名 and 有意思, 有 plus a noun makes an adjective. 没用 is the opposite: 这个办法很有用, 那个办法没用. 没用 can also put down a person as hopeless.
column9: Like 有名 and 有意思, 有 plus a noun makes an adjective. 沒用 is the opposite: 這個辦法很有用, 那個辦法沒用. 沒用 can also put down a person as hopeless.

column3: Something comes to you, often not a physical object: 得到帮助, 得到机会, 得到答案. For something physical, 拿到 and 买到 are common. Its old form is a hand picking up a cowry shell: to obtain valuables. 得 is read dé here, “to obtain”.
column6: Tā dédào le lǎoshī de bāngzhù.
column7: He got help from the teacher.
column9: Something comes to you, often not a physical object: 得到幫助, 得到機會, 得到答案. For something physical, 拿到 and 買到 are common. Its old form is a hand picking up a cowry shell: to obtain valuables. 得 is read dé here, “to obtain”.

column3: Give back, return: 还书 "return books", 还钱 "pay back". The same character is also hái "still". 辶 (walk) is the meaning part.
column9: Give back, return: 還書 "return books", 還錢 "pay back". The same character is also hái "still". 辶 (walk) is the meaning part.

column3: Which noun takes it is learned phrase by phrase: 打电话, 打伞 (hold an umbrella), 打针 (get a shot). Ball games you hit or throw take 打, as in 打篮球, while kicked ones take 踢: 踢足球.
column9: Which noun takes it is learned phrase by phrase: 打電話, 打傘 (hold an umbrella), 打針 (get a shot). Ball games you hit or throw take 打, as in 打籃球, while kicked ones take 踢: 踢足球.

column3: Open, "turn on", "start, run": 开门 "open the door", 开车 "drive", 开会 "hold a meeting". The opposite is 关: 关门 "close the door", 关灯 "turn off the light".
column9: Open, "turn on", "start, run": 開門 "open the door", 開車 "drive", 開會 "hold a meeting". The opposite is 關: 關門 "close the door", 關燈 "turn off the light".

column3: Pairs with 开 for doors, lights and devices: 关门 and 开门, 关灯 and 开灯. 关 names the act; 关上 says the result, that it is now shut. The old form is a door locked with two wooden sticks, and the simplified form drops the door.
column9: Pairs with 開 for doors, lights and devices: 關門 and 開門, 關燈 and 開燈. 關 names the act; 關上 says the result, that it is now shut. The old form is a door locked with two wooden sticks.

column3: 上 after a verb says the action ends up closed or attached: 关上, 盖上 (put a lid on), 穿上 (put on). The negative says it will not close: 门关不上。
column9: 上 after a verb says the action ends up closed or attached: 關上, 蓋上 (put a lid on), 穿上 (put on). The negative says it will not close: 門關不上。

column3: It opens a door, a book, a file or a lid, and turns on a screen: 打开电视, 打开手机. For lights, plain 开灯 is usual. The opposite is 关上. The old form of 开 shows a pair of hands opening a latched door.
column9: It opens a door, a book, a file or a lid, and turns on a screen: 打開電視, 打開手機. For lights, plain 開燈 is usual. The opposite is 關上. The old form of 開 shows a pair of hands opening a latched door.

column3: Mostly a building block of longer words: 运动, 动物, 行动, 感动. On its own it turns up in 别动 (don't move) and 动不了 (cannot be moved).
column9: Mostly a building block of longer words: 運動, 動物, 行動, 感動. On its own it turns up in 別動 (don't move) and 動不了 (cannot be moved).

column3: A physical movement, a gesture or a step, as in exercise, dance or a martial art: 动作很快, 动作标准 (correct form). It is also a move taken by a company or government: 有新动作. For taking action, say 行动.
column9: A physical movement, a gesture or a step, as in exercise, dance or a martial art: 動作很快, 動作標準 (correct form). It is also a move taken by a company or government: 有新動作. For taking action, say 行動.

column3: It also gives and asks age: 你多大了？ and 他比我大两岁. With a noun it needs no 的: 大房子, 大学. It began as a picture of a standing person facing forward.
column9: It also gives and asks age: 你多大了？ and 他比我大兩歲. With a noun it needs no 的: 大房子, 大學. It began as a picture of a standing person facing forward.

column3: Before a surname it is a friendly way to address a younger person or peer: 小王. It adds affection to young creatures and people: 小狗, 小孩. The opposite is 大. It is three small dots, and one view takes them for three grains of sand.
column6: Zhè ge bēizi tài xiǎo le.
column9: Before a surname it is a friendly way to address a younger person or peer: 小王. It adds affection to young creatures and people: 小狗, 小孩. The opposite is 大. It is three small dots, and one view takes them for three grains of sand.

column3: Tall, high: 他很高. It is a picture of a tall building. For comparison, 他比我高 "he is taller than me".
column9: Tall, high: 他很高. It is a picture of a tall building. For comparison, 他比我高 "he is taller than me".

column3: It goes straight before a noun: 新书, 新房子. It builds 新年, 新闻 (news) and 新鲜 (fresh). The opposite is 旧.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī ge xīn bēizi.
column9: It goes straight before a noun: 新書, 新房子. It builds 新年, 新聞 (news) and 新鮮 (fresh). The opposite is 舊.

column3: Also a friendly prefix before a surname or nickname (老王, 老张), and before a number for birth order (老二 is the second child). For things that are simply not new, 旧 is the word; 老 suits people and long-standing things like 老店. It shows an old man with long hair leaning on a cane.
column6: Tā shì wǒ de lǎo péngyou.
column9: Also a friendly prefix before a surname or nickname (老王, 老張), and before a number for birth order (老二 is the second child). For things that are simply not new, 舊 is the word; 老 suits people and long-standing things like 老店. It shows an old man with long hair leaning on a cane.

column3: After a verb or adjective it means 'to the point of ruin': 累坏了 is worn out, 气坏了 is furious. Alone it is the opposite of 好, for things and for people (坏人, 坏消息). Earth is the meaning part because what rots eventually goes back to earth.
column9: After a verb or adjective it means 'to the point of ruin': 累壞了 is worn out, 氣壞了 is furious. Alone it is the opposite of 好, for things and for people (壞人, 壞消息). Earth is the meaning part because what rots eventually goes back to earth.

column3: With 了 it means 'about to': 快到了 (almost there), 快下雨了 (it's about to rain). 快点儿 urges someone to hurry up, and the opposite of 快 is 慢.
column9: With 了 it means 'about to': 快到了 (almost there), 快下雨了 (it's about to rain). 快點兒 urges someone to hurry up, and the opposite of 快 is 慢.

column3: 慢走 is a polite goodbye to a guest who is leaving, like 'take care'. 慢点儿 asks someone to slow down, and 慢慢来 means 'take your time'.
column6: Nǐ zǒu de tài màn le.
column9: 慢走 is a polite goodbye to a guest who is leaving, like 'take care'. 慢點兒 asks someone to slow down, and 慢慢來 means 'take your time'.

column3: Before a verb it says the action is hard or unpleasant: 难写, 难懂, 难吃, 难听, 难看. It works like 好 plus a verb, but with the opposite feeling.
column7: Chinese characters are hard to write.
column9: Before a verb it says the action is hard or unpleasant: 難寫, 難懂, 難吃, 難聽, 難看. It works like 好 plus a verb, but with the opposite feeling.

column3: Said of prices, opposite 便宜: 太贵了 is a common bargaining line. It is also an honorific for the other person: 贵姓 asks 'your surname?' and 贵公司 means 'your company'.
column9: Said of prices, opposite 便宜: 太貴了 is a common bargaining line. It is also an honorific for the other person: 貴姓 asks 'your surname?' and 貴公司 means 'your company'.

column3: Besides the color it means 'in vain' and 'for free': 白跑一趟 is a wasted trip, 白吃 is eating without paying. It also means 'plain' in 白饭 and 白开水.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì bái de.
column7: This piece of clothing is white.
column9: Besides the color it means 'in vain' and 'for free': 白跑一趟 is a wasted trip, 白吃 is eating without paying. It also means 'plain' in 白飯 and 白開水.

column3: Said of weight (很重) and of seriousness (重病 is a serious illness, 重要 important). 重 is a common start of compounds: 重量 weight, 重点 the main point. It began as a man carrying a bag, with 土 added later to show him standing on the ground.
column9: Said of weight (很重) and of seriousness (重病 is a serious illness, 重要 important). 重 is a common start of compounds: 重量 weight, 重點 the main point. It began as a man carrying a bag, with 土 added later to show him standing on the ground.

column3: Dry (gān): 衣服干了 "the clothes are dry". 干杯 "cheers" means "dry the cup". The opposite is 湿 "wet".
column9: Dry (gān): 衣服乾了 "the clothes are dry". 乾杯 "cheers" means "dry the cup". The opposite is 溼 "wet".

column3: After a verb it gives the result: 洗干净 (wash clean), 擦干净 (wipe clean). Before a noun it needs 的: 干净的衣服. The opposite is 脏.
column9: After a verb it gives the result: 洗乾淨 (wash clean), 擦乾淨 (wipe clean). Before a noun it needs 的: 乾淨的衣服. The opposite is 髒.

column3: For the clock it means 'short of': 差五分三点 is five to three, also said 三点差五分. For quality it is the opposite of 好: 成绩差, 他的汉语很差.
column6: Xiànzài chà wǔ fēn sān diǎn.
column9: For the clock it means 'short of': 差五分三點 is five to three, also said 三點差五分. For quality it is the opposite of 好: 成績差, 他的漢語很差.

column3: 离 names the point you measure from: 我家离学校很远 (home is far from school). The opposite is 近. It also strengthens a comparison: 远比…好 means 'far better than'.
column6: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn yuǎn.
column7: My home is far from school.
column9: 離 names the point you measure from: 我家離學校很遠 (home is far from school). The opposite is 近. It also strengthens a comparison: 遠比…好 means 'far better than'.

column3: Follows the 有 plus noun pattern for 'having that quality', as in 有用, 有钱, 有意思. Used of people, places, shops and dishes; 著名 is the more formal 'famous' of news writing.
column9: Follows the 有 plus noun pattern for 'having that quality', as in 有用, 有錢, 有意思. Used of people, places, shops and dishes; 著名 is the more formal 'famous' of news writing.

column3: Works as a predicate (很重要) or before a noun (重要的事). 重要的是… introduces the main point: 重要的是努力, 'what matters is effort'.
column9: Works as a predicate (很重要) or before a noun (重要的事). 重要的是… introduces the main point: 重要的是努力, 'what matters is effort'.

column3: Describes an attitude, before a verb (认真听, 认真学习) or after 得 (学得很认真). It can also mean 'take it seriously': 别太认真 is 'don't take it so seriously'.
column9: Describes an attitude, before a verb (認真聽, 認真學習) or after 得 (學得很認真). It can also mean 'take it seriously': 別太認真 is 'don't take it so seriously'.

column3: Also means health: 身体好, 身体不好. 注意身体 is a common parting wish, 'look after yourself', and 您身体好吗 asks politely after someone's health. 身 began as a picture of a pregnant woman.
column9: Also means health: 身體好, 身體不好. 注意身體 is a common parting wish, 'look after yourself', and 您身體好嗎 asks politely after someone's health. 身 began as a picture of a pregnant woman.

column3: Used for what someone carries or wears: 身上带着, 身上穿着. Also for what happens to a person or what a person has in them: 事情发生在他身上, 他身上有很多优点.
column7: I have no money on me.
column9: Used for what someone carries or wears: 身上帶著, 身上穿著. Also for what happens to a person or what a person has in them: 事情發生在他身上, 他身上有很多優點.

column3: Also names a person skilled at something: 歌手 (singer), 选手 (player), 助手 (assistant). As a prefix it means 'by hand' or 'handheld': 手写, 手机.
column9: Also names a person skilled at something: 歌手 (singer), 選手 (player), 助手 (assistant). As a prefix it means 'by hand' or 'handheld': 手寫, 手機.

column3: Mouth, and the measure word for family members: 四口人. Also "opening": 门口, 路口. It is an open mouth. Keep it apart from 日 (sun), which has a stroke inside.
column6: Tā jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
column7: There are three people in his family.
column9: Mouth, and the measure word for family members: 四口人. Also "opening": 門口, 路口. It is an open mouth. Keep it apart from 日 (sun), which has a stroke inside.

column3: Illness: 他的病好了 "his illness has gone". Also "to be ill": 他病了. 疒 (sickness) is the meaning part and 丙 the sound (bǐng, close to bìng).
column7: He has recovered from his illness.
column9: Illness: 他的病好了 "his illness has gone". Also "to be ill": 他病了. 疒 (sickness) is the meaning part and 丙 the sound (bǐng, close to bìng).

column3: Said from either side: a patient goes to 看病 (去医院看病), a doctor 看病 for patients. To visit a sick friend, say 看望 or 探病, not 看病.
column7: I'm going to the hospital to see a doctor tomorrow.
column9: Said from either side: a patient goes to 看病 (去醫院看病), a doctor 看病 for patients. To visit a sick friend, say 看望 or 探病, not 看病.

column3: A verb plus its object, so 了 can split it: 生了一场病 'came down with an illness'. 生 here is 'come about', not 'be born'; 病了 alone says much the same.
column9: A verb plus its object, so 了 can split it: 生了一場病 'came down with an illness'. 生 here is 'come about', not 'be born'; 病了 alone says much the same.

column3: Covers tired bodies and tiring work: 我很累, 累死了 (dead tired), 工作很累. It can also be a verb: 别累着 'don't wear yourself out'.
column9: Covers tired bodies and tiring work: 我很累, 累死了 (dead tired), 工作很累. It can also be a verb: 別累著 'don't wear yourself out'.

column3: 睡着 means 'fall asleep' (孩子睡着了), while 睡 alone is just 'sleep'. 睡醒 is 'wake up', and 睡得好 'sleep well'.
column9: 睡著 means 'fall asleep' (孩子睡著了), while 睡 alone is just 'sleep'. 睡醒 is 'wake up', and 睡得好 'sleep well'.

column3: A verb plus its object, so it splits: 睡了一觉 (had a sleep), 睡不着觉 (can't sleep). 去睡觉 is the usual way to say 'go to bed'. 觉 is read jiào in 睡觉.
column7: I go to bed at ten.
column9: A verb plus its object, so it splits: 睡了一覺 (had a sleep), 睡不著覺 (can't sleep). 去睡覺 is the usual way to say 'go to bed'. 覺 is read jiào in 睡覺.

column3: A state you are in: 我饿了, 饿死了 (starving), 肚子饿. Its opposite is 饱, as in 我吃饱了. 又饿又渴 is 'both hungry and thirsty'.
column6: Wǒ è le, wǒmen chīfàn ba.
column9: A state you are in: 我餓了, 餓死了 (starving), 肚子餓. Its opposite is 飽, as in 我吃飽了. 又餓又渴 is 'both hungry and thirsty'.

column3: Used as 我渴了 or 口渴, and 渴死了 for 'dying of thirst'. It stretches to longing, as in 渴望 (to long for).
column6: Wǒ hěn kě, xiǎng hē shuǐ.
column7: I'm very thirsty, I want some water.
column9: Used as 我渴了 or 口渴, and 渴死了 for 'dying of thirst'. It stretches to longing, as in 渴望 (to long for).

column3: Mostly the start of other words: 电话, 电脑, 电视, 电影, 电梯 (elevator), 电池 (battery). Alone it is the power: 手机没电了 means the phone is out of charge.
column7: The power is out at home.
column9: Mostly the start of other words: 電話, 電腦, 電視, 電影, 電梯 (elevator), 電池 (battery). Alone it is the power: 手機沒電了 means the phone is out of charge.

column3: Verbs that go with it: 打电话 (make a call), 接电话 (answer), 挂电话 (hang up). It means the phone and the call; 电话号码 is a phone number.
column6: Nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ shì duōshao?
column9: Verbs that go with it: 打電話 (make a call), 接電話 (answer), 掛電話 (hang up). It means the phone and the call; 電話號碼 is a phone number.

column3: The everyday word for a desktop or laptop computer; a laptop is 笔记本电脑 on the mainland and 笔电 in Taiwan. Verbs: 开电脑 (turn on), 关电脑 (shut down), 用电脑 (use).
column9: The everyday word for a desktop or laptop computer; a laptop is 筆記本電腦 on the mainland and 筆電 in Taiwan. Verbs: 開電腦 (turn on), 關電腦 (shut down), 用電腦 (use).

column3: Both the set and television as a medium: 看电视 (watch TV), 开电视 (turn it on), 电视节目 (TV show), 电视剧 (TV drama). The machine itself is 电视机.
column9: Both the set and television as a medium: 看電視 (watch TV), 開電視 (turn it on), 電視節目 (TV show), 電視劇 (TV drama). The machine itself is 電視機.

column3: The machine itself, so it takes 买, 修 and 坏了, while watching is 看电视, never 看电视机. 机 is the machine in 手机, 洗衣机 and the aircraft in 飞机.
column9: The machine itself, so it takes 買, 修 and 壞了, while watching is 看電視, never 看電視機. 機 is the machine in 手機, 洗衣機 and the aircraft in 飛機.

column3: Counted with 部: 一部电影. Verbs: 看电影 (watch), 拍电影 (make a film). 去看电影 is the usual way to suggest a movie outing. 影 first meant 'shadow'.
column7: Do you want to watch a movie?
column9: Counted with 部: 一部電影. Verbs: 看電影 (watch), 拍電影 (make a film). 去看電影 is the usual way to suggest a movie outing. 影 first meant 'shadow'.

column3: The everyday word for a cell phone. Verbs: 用手机, 玩手机, 给手机充电 (charge it). 手机号 is a cell phone number, and 手机没电了 means it is out of battery.
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī zài zhuōzi shang.
column7: My phone is on the table.
column9: The everyday word for a cell phone. Verbs: 用手機, 玩手機, 給手機充電 (charge it). 手機號 is a cell phone number, and 手機沒電了 means it is out of battery.

column3: The person called goes before the verb: 给他打电话 'call him', or after: 打电话给他. 打 is a light verb here, as in 打车 and 打球.
column9: The person called goes before the verb: 給他打電話 'call him', or after: 打電話給他. 打 is a light verb here, as in 打車 and 打球.

column3: A verb plus its object, so it splits: 上了网, 上不了网 (can't get online). 上网看新闻 reads the news online, and 网上 means 'on the Internet': 网上购物.
column7: I go online in the evening.
column9: A verb plus its object, so it splits: 上了網, 上不了網 (can't get online). 上網看新聞 reads the news online, and 網上 means 'on the Internet': 網上購物.

column3: Online, on the internet: 网上买东西 "shop online". As a place word, it follows 在 and comes before the verb.
column9: Online, on the internet: 網上買東西 "shop online". As a place word, it follows 在 and comes before the verb.

column3: Counted with 首: 一首歌. It joins 唱歌 (sing), 歌手 (singer) and 歌词 (lyrics).
column9: Counted with 首: 一首歌. It joins 唱歌 (sing), 歌手 (singer) and 歌詞 (lyrics).

column3: Covers children's play, outings and hanging out: 去哪儿玩儿, 玩手机, 玩得开心. The 儿 ending is northern speech; in the south and in Taiwan it is just 玩.
column9: Covers children's play, outings and hanging out: 去哪兒玩兒, 玩手機, 玩得開心. The 兒 ending is northern speech; in the south and in Taiwan it is just 玩.

column3: Follows the 好 plus verb pattern of 好吃, 好看, 好用. Said of places, games and activities: 这个游戏很好玩儿. For a funny person, 有意思 or 有趣 is more usual.
column9: Follows the 好 plus verb pattern of 好吃, 好看, 好用. Said of places, games and activities: 這個遊戲很好玩兒. For a funny person, 有意思 or 有趣 is more usual.

column3: A verb plus its object: 跟他开玩笑 (joke with him), 开他的玩笑 (make fun of him). 别开玩笑了 means 'stop kidding', and 你开玩笑吧 'you must be joking'.
column9: A verb plus its object: 跟他開玩笑 (joke with him), 開他的玩笑 (make fun of him). 別開玩笑了 means 'stop kidding', and 你開玩笑吧 'you must be joking'.

column3: Sports are 球 compounds: 足球 (soccer), 篮球, 网球, 乒乓球. Alone it is a ball or the game of ball; 地球 is the Earth.
column9: Sports are 球 compounds: 足球 (soccer), 籃球, 網球, 乒乓球. Alone it is a ball or the game of ball; 地球 is the Earth.

column3: Covers games played with the hands or a racket, such as basketball and tennis. Soccer is 踢球, 'kick the ball'.
column7: We play ball in the afternoon.
column9: Covers games played with the hands or a racket, such as basketball and tennis. Soccer is 踢球, 'kick the ball'.

column3: Ends country names: 中国, 美国, 英国, 法国. 外国 is foreign (外国人), and 哪国人 asks what country someone is from. Alone it is mostly bound in compounds.
column9: Ends country names: 中國, 美國, 英國, 法國. 外國 is foreign (外國人), and 哪國人 asks what country someone is from. Alone it is mostly bound in compounds.

column3: The general word, as in 每个国家, also 'national': 国家队, 国家公园. A named country ends in 国, not 国家 (中国, 美国), and its people add 人: 美国人.
column6: Nǐ qù guo jǐ ge guójiā?
column7: How many countries have you been to?
column9: The general word, as in 每個國家, also 'national': 國家隊, 國家公園. A named country ends in 國, not 國家 (中國, 美國), and its people add 人: 美國人.

column3: A place word: 去国外, 在国外. To describe things as foreign use 外国: 外国人, 外国朋友. The opposite of 国外 is 国内.
column9: A place word: 去國外, 在國外. To describe things as foreign use 外國: 外國人, 外國朋友. The opposite of 國外 is 國內.

column3: Foreign country, before a noun "foreign": 外国朋友, 外国人. Compare 国外 "abroad", which is a place.
column6: Wǒ yǒu hěn duō wàiguó péngyou.
column9: Foreign country, before a noun "foreign": 外國朋友, 外國人. Compare 國外 "abroad", which is a place.

column3: A Chinese person is 中国人. The language is 中文 or 汉语, and its writing is 汉字.
column9: A Chinese person is 中國人. The language is 中文 or 漢語, and its writing is 漢字.

column3: Beijing: 北 ("north") plus 京 ("capital", as in 京城). 京 is a picture of a tall building. From 1928 to 1949, when it was not the capital, it was called 北平. A proper name, so the pinyin is capitalized.
column9: Beijing: 北 ("north") plus 京 ("capital", as in 京城). 京 is a picture of a tall building. From 1928 to 1949, when it was not the capital, it was called 北平. A proper name, so the pinyin is capitalized.

column3: Shop, store: 去商店; 一家商店. 店 has 广 (a building) as meaning part and 占 (zhàn) as sound part, the same 占 as in 点 and 站.
column7: What time does the shop close?
column9: Shop, store: 去商店; 一家商店. 店 has 广 (a building) as meaning part and 占 (zhàn) as sound part, the same 占 as in 點 and 站.

column3: A mall or large store with many shops, where you 逛商场 (stroll around) or 去商场买东西. A single shop is a 商店.
column7: We're going to the mall to buy clothes.
column9: A mall or large store with many shops, where you 逛商場 (stroll around) or 去商場買東西. A single shop is a 商店.

column3: 去医院 is the everyday way to say you are seeing a doctor. A small clinic is a 诊所. 院 ends many institutions: 医院, 电影院, 学院, 法院.
column9: 去醫院 is the everyday way to say you are seeing a doctor. A small clinic is a 診所. 院 ends many institutions: 醫院, 電影院, 學院, 法院.

column3: The shorter 影院 is common in the names of theaters. 在电影院看电影 means watching a movie in a theater; 院 is the same 院 as in 医院.
column7: Let's meet at the movie theater.
column9: The shorter 影院 is common in the names of theaters. 在電影院看電影 means watching a movie in a theater; 院 is the same 院 as in 醫院.

column3: Ground and land: 土地, 地图, 地球 (the Earth). The subway is 地铁 on the mainland and 捷运 in Taiwan.
column7: This piece of land is big.
column9: Ground and land: 土地, 地圖, 地球 (the Earth). The subway is 地鐵 on the mainland and 捷運 in Taiwan.

column3: A place: 什么地方, 好地方. Also a part or aspect: 这个地方我没看懂 means 'I didn't understand this part', and 有些地方不一样 'it differs in some respects'.
column9: A place: 什麼地方, 好地方. Also a part or aspect: 這個地方我沒看懂 means 'I didn't understand this part', and 有些地方不一樣 'it differs in some respects'.

column3: The location of an event or meeting, more specific than 地方: 开会地点, 比赛地点, 时间和地点. In everyday speech, asking 'where' uses 在哪儿, not 地点.
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ shíjiān hé dìdiǎn.
column7: Please tell me the time and place.
column9: The location of an event or meeting, more specific than 地方: 開會地點, 比賽地點, 時間和地點. In everyday speech, asking 'where' uses 在哪兒, not 地點.

column3: Used with 在, 坐 and 掉: 坐在地上 (sit on the floor), 掉在地上 (fall to the ground). 地下 means underground, as in 地下室 (basement); in the north it also means 'on the floor', as in 掉地下了.
column7: The book is on the floor.
column9: Used with 在, 坐 and 掉: 坐在地上 (sit on the floor), 掉在地上 (fall to the ground). 地下 means underground, as in 地下室 (basement); in the north it also means 'on the floor', as in 掉地下了.

column3: The measure word is 张, and a place is found on it with 在地图上. Kinds are named in front: 世界地图, 中国地图, 旅游地图.
column9: The measure word is 張, and a place is found on it with 在地圖上. Kinds are named in front: 世界地圖, 中國地圖, 旅遊地圖.

column3: Restaurant on the mainland. In Taiwan it usually means "hotel", and some famous mainland hotels have it in their names, such as 北京饭店. 饭 ("meal") plus 店 ("shop").
column6: Zhè ge fàndiàn de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food at this restaurant is delicious.
column9: Restaurant on the mainland. In Taiwan it usually means "hotel", and some famous mainland hotels have it in their names, such as 北京飯店. 飯 ("meal") plus 店 ("shop").

column3: Bookshop: 书 plus 店. 在书店买书 "buy books at the bookshop".
column7: The bookshop is next to the school.
column9: Bookshop: 書 plus 店. 在書店買書 "buy books at the bookshop".

column3: A public or school library, where you borrow books (借书) and study. A bookstore is a different word, 书店.
column9: A public or school library, where you borrow books (借書) and study. A bookstore is a different word, 書店.

column3: The general word for any wheeled vehicle, so context decides: 开车 for a car, 骑车 for a bike. Many words end in it: 汽车, 火车, 自行车. The measure word is 辆. It began as a picture of a carriage seen from above, and the oldest forms show large wheels on both sides.
column6: Chē lái le, kuài shàng chē.
column7: The bus is here, get on quickly.
column9: The general word for any wheeled vehicle, so context decides: 開車 for a car, 騎車 for a bike. Many words end in it: 汽車, 火車, 自行車. The measure word is 輛. It began as a picture of a carriage seen from above, and the oldest forms show large wheels on both sides.

column3: Used for a car, and for a long-distance bus too, as in 汽车站. The measure word is 辆; a city bus is 公共汽车. 汽 means vapor or gas, as in 汽油 (gasoline) and 汽水 (soda).
column9: Used for a car, and for a long-distance bus too, as in 汽車站. The measure word is 輛; a city bus is 公共汽車. 汽 means vapor or gas, as in 汽油 (gasoline) and 汽水 (soda).

column3: Said for any train, fast or slow; a high-speed train is 高铁. You ride it with 坐, and it goes from a 火车站. The 火 is a fire: the first trains ran on steam from a fire.
column7: What time does the train arrive?
column9: Said for any train, fast or slow; a high-speed train is 高鐵. You ride it with 坐, and it goes from a 火車站. The 火 is a fire: the first trains ran on steam from a fire.

column3: 机 stands for a machine or aircraft in words like 直升机 (helicopter), 机场 and 机票. The measure word is 架, and you go by plane with 坐飞机.
column9: 機 stands for a machine or aircraft in words like 直升機 (helicopter), 機場 and 機票. The measure word is 架, and you go by plane with 坐飛機.

column3: A verb that takes a destination straight after it (飞北京) or 飞到 it. Related words: 起飞 for taking off, 降落 for landing, 飞机 for the plane. It began as a picture of a bird flying upwards.
column9: A verb that takes a destination straight after it (飛北京) or 飛到 it. Related words: 起飛 for taking off, 降落 for landing, 飛機 for the plane. It began as a picture of a bird flying upwards.

column3: A stop or station for buses and trains alike, so it comes with a type in front: 火车站, 汽车站. A city bus stop is 公交站 on the mainland and 公车站 in Taiwan; a subway stop is 地铁站 on the mainland and 捷运站 in Taiwan.
column7: There are a lot of people at the station.
column9: A stop or station for buses and trains alike, so it comes with a type in front: 火車站, 汽車站. A city bus stop is 公交站 on the mainland and 公車站 in Taiwan; a subway stop is 地鐵站 on the mainland and 捷運站 in Taiwan.

column3: A place word meaning in the car or aboard the bus or train. It follows 在 and needs no extra "inside": 在车上.
column7: My book is in the car.
column9: A place word meaning in the car or aboard the bus or train. It follows 在 and needs no extra "inside": 在車上.

column3: The ticket you buy for a trip by bus or train, counted with 张: 买车票. Tickets are checked with 检票 at the gate or 查票 on board. A plane ticket is a 机票.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng chēpiào.
column9: The ticket you buy for a trip by bus or train, counted with 張: 買車票. Tickets are checked with 檢票 at the gate or 查票 on board. A plane ticket is a 機票.

column3: Airport: 机 ("plane") plus 场 ("open ground"). 去机场; 机场很大.
column7: I'm waiting for you at the airport.
column9: Airport: 機 ("plane") plus 場 ("open ground"). 去機場; 機場很大.

column3: Booked and bought online or at a counter: 订机票, 买机票, 退机票 for a refund. The measure word is 张, and a one-way flight is 单程机票, a round trip 往返机票.
column7: The plane ticket is too expensive.
column9: Booked and bought online or at a counter: 訂機票, 買機票, 退機票 for a refund. The measure word is 張, and a one-way flight is 單程機票, a round trip 往返機票.

column3: 票 is the base of many ticket words: 车票, 机票, 门票, 电影票. It also means a ballot, as in 投票 "to vote". The measure word is 张.
column9: 票 is the base of many ticket words: 車票, 機票, 門票, 電影票. It also means a ballot, as in 投票 "to vote". The measure word is 張.

column3: The ticket to get into a park, museum or show, counted with 张; its price is asked with 门票多少钱. Free entry is 免费开放 or 不要门票; 免费门票 is a complimentary ticket handed out.
column7: An admission ticket is twenty yuan.
column9: The ticket to get into a park, museum or show, counted with 張; its price is asked with 門票多少錢. Free entry is 免費開放 or 不要門票; 免費門票 is a complimentary ticket handed out.

column3: A verb and its object, so it can split: 上了车, 上不了车. It is for a car, bus or train; for a plane, say 上飞机 in speech, and 登机 is the word on signs and announcements. Its opposite is 下车.
column9: A verb and its object, so it can split: 上了車, 上不了車. It is for a car, bus or train; for a plane, say 上飛機 in speech, and 登機 is the word on signs and announcements. Its opposite is 下車.

column3: A verb and its object, so 了 goes after the verb: 下了车. The stop you leave at goes before it: 在哪儿下车, 在下一站下车.
column9: A verb and its object, so 了 goes after the verb: 下了車. The stop you leave at goes before it: 在哪兒下車, 在下一站下車.
