column3: Road: 马路, 走路; also a route, as of a bus: 三路车. 足 (foot) is the meaning part and 各 the sound (gè against lù).
column9: Road: 馬路, 走路; also a route, as of a bus: 三路車. 足 (foot) is the meaning part and 各 the sound (gè against lù).

column3: Where roads meet, whether a crossroads or a simple junction. Directions use it: 前面的路口, 在下一个路口左转 "turn left at the next intersection"; the lights are 红绿灯.
column9: Where roads meet, whether a crossroads or a simple junction. Directions use it: 前面的路口, 在下一個路口左轉 "turn left at the next intersection"; the lights are 紅綠燈.

column3: A time word as well as a place: while you are traveling, whether by car, on foot or on a trip. 路上小心 is said to someone leaving, and 路上堵车 is a jam on the way.
column9: A time word as well as a place: while you are traveling, whether by car, on foot or on a trip. 路上小心 is said to someone leaving, and 路上堵車 is a jam on the way.

column3: A street or road for traffic, in a city or the country; the contrast is with a path, 小路. You cross it with 过马路, at a crosswalk (斑马线).
column9: A street or road for traffic, in a city or the country; the contrast is with a path, 小路. You cross it with 過馬路, at a crosswalk (斑馬線).

column3: A verb and its object, so a length or amount goes between: 开了一个小时的车. Driving yourself is 开车; hailing a taxi is 打车, and riding as a passenger is 坐车.
column9: A verb and its object, so a length or amount goes between: 開了一個小時的車. Driving yourself is 開車; hailing a taxi is 打車, and riding as a passenger is 坐車.

column3: To get a taxi on the mainland, now often with an app (打车软件); in Taiwan say 搭计程车 or 叫车. You are the passenger; to drive yourself, say 开车.
column9: To get a taxi on the mainland, now often with an app (打車軟件); in Taiwan say 搭計程車 or 叫車. You are the passenger; to drive yourself, say 開車.

column3: The everyday word for clothes, counted with 件: 一件衣服. The verbs are 穿 to put on or wear, 脱 to take off and 洗 to wash.
column7: This piece of clothing is expensive.
column9: The everyday word for clothes, counted with 件: 一件衣服. The verbs are 穿 to put on or wear, 脫 to take off and 洗 to wash.

column3: 穿 is for what goes on the body or feet: 衣服, 裤子, 鞋, 袜子. A hat, glasses or a watch take 戴 instead. Its opposite is 脱, and 穿上 is to put on. It is 穴 over 牙, meaning to go through, which is why 穿 also means to pierce or pass through.
column9: 穿 is for what goes on the body or feet: 衣服, 褲子, 鞋, 襪子. A hat, glasses or a watch take 戴 instead. Its opposite is 脫, and 穿上 is to put on. It is 穴 over 牙, meaning to go through, which is why 穿 also means to pierce or pass through.

column3: Used for washing and bathing alike: 洗手, 洗脸, 洗澡, 洗衣服, 洗碗. A thing washed clean is 洗干净.
column7: I'm going to wash my hands.
column9: Used for washing and bathing alike: 洗手, 洗臉, 洗澡, 洗衣服, 洗碗. A thing washed clean is 洗乾淨.

column3: Weather is described with 好, 坏, 热, 冷, and asked about with 天气怎么样. A forecast is 天气预报. Weather is a thing you talk about; rain and wind come as verbs: 下雨, 刮风.
column9: Weather is described with 好, 壞, 熱, 冷, and asked about with 天氣怎麼樣. A forecast is 天氣預報. Weather is a thing you talk about; rain and wind come as verbs: 下雨, 颳風.

column3: Rain takes 下: 下雨, 下大雨. The kinds are 大雨 and 小雨, and an umbrella is 雨伞. It began as a picture of a cloud with drops falling from it.
column6: Yǔ hěn dà, bié chūqù le.
column7: The rain is heavy, so don't go out.
column9: Rain takes 下: 下雨, 下大雨. The kinds are 大雨 and 小雨, and an umbrella is 雨傘. It began as a picture of a cloud with drops falling from it.

column3: A verb and its object with no subject, so 了 can show it has begun: 下雨了. How hard is said first: 下大雨, 下小雨. Its mirror is 下雪.
column9: A verb and its object with no subject, so 了 can show it has begun: 下雨了. How hard is said first: 下大雨, 下小雨. Its mirror is 下雪.

column3: The wind is strong or weak (风大, 风小); it blows with 刮风 and the wind 吹. Bigger weather is named by it: 台风 for a typhoon, and 风 is in 风景 too.
column9: The wind is strong or weak (風大, 風小); it blows with 颳風 and the wind 吹. Bigger weather is named by it: 颱風 for a typhoon, and 風 is in 風景 too.

column3: A mountain or hill, counted with 座. Place names often end in it (泰山, 黄山), and 山上 is on a mountain; 爬山 is to hike up one. It began as a picture of three mountain peaks.
column9: A mountain or hill, counted with 座. Place names often end in it (泰山, 黃山), and 山上 is on a mountain; 爬山 is to hike up one. It began as a picture of three mountain peaks.

column3: Trees are counted with 棵: 一棵树. Parts and groups are 树叶, 树枝 and 树林, and 种树 is to plant them.
column6: Shān shang yǒu hěn duō shù.
column7: There are many trees on the mountain.
column9: Trees are counted with 棵: 一棵樹. Parts and groups are 樹葉, 樹枝 and 樹林, and 種樹 is to plant them.

column3: Flower, and "to spend": 花钱 "spend money". 艹 (plant) is the meaning part and 化 the sound, huà against huā.
column9: Flower, and "to spend": 花錢 "spend money". 艹 (plant) is the meaning part and 化 the sound, huà against huā.

column3: Hot for weather, water and food: 天气热, 热水, 热汤. 烫 is for something too hot to touch. It also means lively in 热闹, and a hot topic is 热门.
column9: Hot for weather, water and food: 天氣熱, 熱水, 熱湯. 燙 is for something too hot to touch. It also means lively in 熱鬧, and a hot topic is 熱門.

column3: Cold for weather and for how you feel: 天气冷, 我很冷. Food that has cooled is 凉, a milder word than 冷, and a cold drink is 冷饮. Its opposite is 热.
column9: Cold for weather and for how you feel: 天氣冷, 我很冷. Food that has cooled is 涼, a milder word than 冷, and a cold drink is 冷飲. Its opposite is 熱.

column3: A verb and its object, so it splits: 上了一天班. It covers going to work and being at work; for a class it is 上课, and the opposite is 下班. 上班族 are office workers.
column9: A verb and its object, so it splits: 上了一天班. It covers going to work and being at work; for a class it is 上課, and the opposite is 下班. 上班族 are office workers.

column3: To leave work for the day, and 下班后 is after work. 上下班高峰 is rush hour. The opposite is 上班.
column7: What time do you finish work?
column9: To leave work for the day, and 下班後 is after work. 上下班高峰 is rush hour. The opposite is 上班.

column3: Both a verb (在银行工作) and a noun (找工作, 工作很忙). Of a machine it means to run properly. For the everyday "go to work" say 上班.
column6: Tā zài yī jiā yínháng gōngzuò.
column9: Both a verb (在銀行工作) and a noun (找工作, 工作很忙). Of a machine it means to run properly. For the everyday "go to work" say 上班.

column3: A verb and its object, so it splits: 开了一个会, 开完会, 开什么会. You say 开会 for both holding and attending a meeting; 参加会议 is the formal "attend".
column7: We have a meeting in the afternoon.
column9: A verb and its object, so it splits: 開了一個會, 開完會, 開什麼會. You say 開會 for both holding and attending a meeting; 參加會議 is the formal "attend".

column3: The measure word is 件: 一件事. 有事 means "I have something on", 没事 "it's nothing", and 出事 "something bad happened". It was built from a hand holding a flag, which stood for carrying out one's job.
column7: What can I do for you?
column9: The measure word is 件: 一件事. 有事 means "I have something on", 沒事 "it's nothing", and 出事 "something bad happened". It was built from a hand holding a flag, which stood for carrying out one's job.

column3: The reply to an apology or thanks, or a way to say you are fine: 你没事吧？ "are you all right?". Also "free": 你明天没事吗？ The 儿 is optional: 没事 means the same.
column7: No problem, no need to thank me.
column9: The reply to an apology or thanks, or a way to say you are fine: 你沒事吧？ "are you all right?". Also "free": 你明天沒事嗎？ The 兒 is optional: 沒事 means the same.

column3: An ordinary adjective that takes 很: 我很忙. What you are busy with follows directly (忙工作) or after 着 (忙着做饭). 你忙吗？ is how to ask if someone has time.
column9: An ordinary adjective that takes 很: 我很忙. What you are busy with follows directly (忙工作) or after 著 (忙著做飯). 你忙嗎？ is how to ask if someone has time.

column3: Prepare, get ready: 准备早饭; 准备 plus a verb is "plan to".
column9: Prepare, get ready: 準備早飯; 準備 plus a verb is "plan to". 備 is read as a person 亻 carrying a quiver, "ready".

column3: 休息一下 is the usual "take a short break"; it also covers resting when you are tired or ill (回家休息). One person's day off is 休息 too (我明天休息); 放假 is time off given to a whole school or company.
column9: 休息一下 is the usual "take a short break"; it also covers resting when you are tired or ill (回家休息). One person's day off is 休息 too (我明天休息); 放假 is time off given to a whole school or company.

column3: A verb and its object, said of a school or company giving time off: 放了三天假. For one person asking for leave, it is 请假.
column7: We have a day off tomorrow.
column9: A verb and its object, said of a school or company giving time off: 放了三天假. For one person asking for leave, it is 請假.

column3: Ask for leave: 请 ("ask for") plus 假 (jià, "vacation"). A verb and its object: 请了一天假 "took a day off". Compare 放假 "to have a holiday", when everyone is off.
column7: I need to ask for leave tomorrow.
column9: Ask for leave: 請 ("ask for") plus 假 (jià, "vacation"). A verb and its object: 請了一天假 "took a day off". Compare 放假 "to have a holiday", when everyone is off.

column3: The pattern is 帮 plus the person plus the verb: 帮我拿, 帮你找. The helped person comes first. 请帮我 on its own is a polite "please help me"; 帮助 is the more formal verb.
column9: The pattern is 幫 plus the person plus the verb: 幫我拿, 幫你找. The helped person comes first. 請幫我 on its own is a polite "please help me"; 幫助 is the more formal verb.

column3: A verb and its object, so no object follows it: say 帮我的忙 or 帮他一个忙, not 帮忙我. 谢谢你帮忙 and 请帮忙 are common; 帮个忙 is the casual "do me a favor".
column9: A verb and its object, so no object follows it: say 幫我的忙 or 幫他一個忙, not 幫忙我. 謝謝你幫忙 and 請幫忙 are common; 幫個忙 is the casual "do me a favor".

column3: For facts and information: 我知道, 我不知道, 谁知道？ For people and places use 认识. 知道了 is also the everyday "got it".
column6: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā de míngzi.
column9: For facts and information: 我知道, 我不知道, 誰知道？ For people and places use 認識. 知道了 is also the everyday "got it".

column3: For a person you have met and a character you can recognize: 认识他, 认识这个字. For a fact, use 知道. As a noun it is "understanding": 有新的认识.
column6: Nǐ rènshi zhè ge zì ma?
column9: For a person you have met and a character you can recognize: 認識他, 認識這個字. For a fact, use 知道. As a noun it is "understanding": 有新的認識.

column3: Mostly met inside words: 记得, 记住 (memorize it), 忘记, 笔记, 日记. As a verb alone it means to jot down: 记一下. The result form 记不住 means "can't hold it in memory".
column6: Wǒ jì bu zhù zhè ge zì.
column9: Mostly met inside words: 記得, 記住 (memorize it), 忘記, 筆記, 日記. As a verb alone it means to jot down: 記一下. The result form 記不住 means "can't hold it in memory".

column3: The memory is still there: 我记得他的名字, 我不记得了. With a verb it means "remember to": 记得关灯. The opposite is 忘了.
column9: The memory is still there: 我記得他的名字, 我不記得了. With a verb it means "remember to": 記得關燈. The opposite is 忘了.

column3: Memorize, remember firmly: 记住这个字. 住 after a verb says the thing stays put. Negative: 记不住 "can't hold it in mind".
column9: Memorize, remember firmly: 記住這個字. 住 after a verb says the thing stays put. Negative: 記不住 "can't hold it in mind".

column3: Usually with 了: 我忘了, 别忘了 "don't forget". It takes an object (忘了带伞) or a verb for what was forgotten to do.
column6: Wǒ wàng le nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ.
column9: Usually with 了: 我忘了, 別忘了 "don't forget". It takes an object (忘了帶傘) or a verb for what was forgotten to do.

column3: Means the same as 忘 and takes an object: 忘记了他的名字, 别忘记关门. In speech 忘了 is the shorter, more common choice; 忘记 sounds a little more careful.
column7: Don't forget to close the door.
column9: Means the same as 忘 and takes an object: 忘記了他的名字, 別忘記關門. In speech 忘了 is the shorter, more common choice; 忘記 sounds a little more careful.

column3: To get the point or the reasoning: 我明白了, 我不明白为什么. For understanding a language or speech, 懂 is the word (听不懂). It is also an adjective, "clear": 说明白. 白 here has the sense "clear; evident", as in 真相大白.
column9: To get the point or the reasoning: 我明白了, 我不明白為什麼. For understanding a language or speech, 懂 is the word (聽不懂). It is also an adjective, "clear": 說明白. 白 here has the sense "clear; evident", as in 真相大白.

column3: Knowledge as facts and learning: 学知识, 有知识, 丰富的知识. A skill or know-how is not 知识 but 技能. 知识分子 means "intellectuals".
column6: Shū lǐ yǒu hěn duō zhīshi.
column7: There is a lot of knowledge in books.
column9: Knowledge as facts and learning: 學知識, 有知識, 豐富的知識. A skill or know-how is not 知識 but 技能. 知識分子 means "intellectuals".

column3: The person or thing waited for follows directly, with no preposition: 等我, 等车, 等一下. It also ends a list (苹果、香蕉等) and works as "by the time": 等你来了，我们就走。
column9: The person or thing waited for follows directly, with no preposition: 等我, 等車, 等一下. It also ends a list (蘋果、香蕉等) and works as "by the time": 等你來了，我們就走。

column3: To look for, or to call on someone: 找朋友, 找工作, 找老师. It also means to give change: 找你五块. 找 alone is the searching; 找到 is finding. The picture of a hand looking for a halberd is only a memory aid, not where the character came from.
column6: Wǒ zài zhǎo wǒ de shǒujī.
column9: To look for, or to call on someone: 找朋友, 找工作, 找老師. It also means to give change: 找你五塊. 找 alone is the searching; 找到 is finding. The picture of a hand looking for a halberd is only a memory aid, not where the character came from.

column3: 找 is the looking, 找到 the result: 找到了 "found it". The negative splits the word: 找不到 "can't find", and 找得到 "can find".
column6: Wǒ zhǎodào wǒ de qiánbāo le.
column9: 找 is the looking, 找到 the result: 找到了 "found it". The negative splits the word: 找不到 "can't find", and 找得到 "can find".

column3: Joins nouns and pronouns only: 我和你, 苹果和香蕉. It cannot join two verbs or two sentences. It also means "with": 我和朋友去。In speech 跟 does the same job.
column6: Wǒ hé wǒ mèimei shì tóngxué.
column7: My younger sister and I are classmates.
column9: Joins nouns and pronouns only: 我和你, 蘋果和香蕉. It cannot join two verbs or two sentences. It also means "with": 我和朋友去。In speech 跟 does the same job.

column3: The spoken partner of 和 for "with" and "and": 跟我来, 跟他说. 跟…一样 means "the same as". As a plain verb it is "to follow": 跟着我.
column9: The spoken partner of 和 for "with" and "and": 跟我來, 跟他說. 跟…一樣 means "the same as". As a plain verb it is "to follow": 跟著我.

column3: From: 从北京来 "come from Beijing"; 从…到… "from … to …". The character is two 人 (people), one following the other.
column6: Wǒ cóng bā diǎn xué dào shí diǎn.
column7: I study from eight to ten.
column9: From: 從北京來 "come from Beijing"; 從…到… "from … to …". The character is two 人 (people), one following the other.

column3: The pattern is A 比 B plus an adjective: 他比我高. Don't add 很 or 非常 to it; 更 or 还 is fine, and a difference follows the adjective: 高三厘米. "Not as tall as" is 没有: 我没有他高.
column9: The pattern is A 比 B plus an adjective: 他比我高. Don't add 很 or 非常 to it; 更 or 還 is fine, and a difference follows the adjective: 高三釐米. "Not as tall as" is 沒有: 我沒有他高.

column3: As a verb it takes two objects: 给我一本书. As a preposition it means "for" or "to" before the verb: 给妈妈买花, 给他打电话.
column6: Wǒ gěi māma mǎi le huā.
column9: As a verb it takes two objects: 給我一本書. As a preposition it means "for" or "to" before the verb: 給媽媽買花, 給他打電話.

column3: It goes before the verb: 一起去, 一起吃饭. 一块儿 is the spoken synonym. 在一起 means "be together" and, of two people, "be a couple". 一起多少钱？ asks the total.
column9: It goes before the verb: 一起去, 一起吃飯. 一塊兒 is the spoken synonym. 在一起 means "be together" and, of two people, "be a couple". 一起多少錢？ asks the total.

column3: The pattern is A 跟 B 一样: 我的书跟你的一样. Add an adjective for "as … as": 跟他一样高. The negative 不一样 is the everyday "different": 我们不一样.
column6: Wǒ de shū gēn nǐ de yīyàng.
column7: My book is the same as yours.
column9: The pattern is A 跟 B 一樣: 我的書跟你的一樣. Add an adjective for "as … as": 跟他一樣高. The negative 不一樣 is the everyday "different": 我們不一樣.

column3: Opens a clause as "in the end" (最后我们都回家了) and sits before a measure word as "last": 最后一个. For a long-awaited "at last", 终于 is the word.
column7: In the end we all went home.
column9: Opens a clause as "in the end" (最後我們都回家了) and sits before a measure word as "last": 最後一個. For a long-awaited "at last", 終於 is the word.

column3: Means "or" in questions (你喝茶还是喝水？); a statement uses 或者. Also "had better" (还是你去吧) and "still" (他还是那么忙).
column6: Nǐ hē chá háishi hē shuǐ?
column7: Do you want tea or water?
column9: Means "or" in questions (你喝茶還是喝水？); a statement uses 或者. Also "had better" (還是你去吧) and "still" (他還是那麼忙).

column3: Adds one more: 还有一本书, or at the end of a list, 苹果、香蕉，还有梨. It also says what remains: 还有三天. 还有吗？ means "anything else?".
column9: Adds one more: 還有一本書, or at the end of a list, 蘋果、香蕉，還有梨. It also says what remains: 還有三天. 還有嗎？ means "anything else?".

column3: It goes before an adjective or verb: 最大, 最喜欢. It is already the superlative, so don't add 很 or 非常.
column9: It goes before an adjective or verb: 最大, 最喜歡. It is already the superlative, so don't add 很 or 非常.

column3: Two uses: "best" (最好的朋友) and, before a verb, "had better" (你最好休息). The warning form is often negative: 最好别去.
column7: You had better go to bed a little earlier.
column9: Two uses: "best" (最好的朋友) and, before a verb, "had better" (你最好休息). The warning form is often negative: 最好別去.

column3: Works alone (还有别的吗？) or before a noun (别的东西, 别的地方). Here 别 means "other", not the "don't" of 别去.
column6: Nǐ hái yǒu biéde shì ma?
column7: Do you have anything else on?
column9: Works alone (還有別的嗎？) or before a noun (別的東西, 別的地方). Here 別 means "other", not the "don't" of 別去.
